<div class="paper-masthead">
<h1 class="paper-title">The collected theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex framework</h1>
<div class="paper-byline">Rouschev, T. · <em>Millennium Solutions</em> · DOI <a href="https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21819217">10.5281/zenodo.21819217</a> · CC BY-NC-ND 4.0</div>
<div class="paper-addr">777 theorems by exhaustion + 187 proved for every value + 15 rfl declarations · 44 sources · content-address <code>cc8d7f8f-b5eb-8cb5-b732-21765bc8e587</code></div>
</div>

<h2 class="paper-h">Abstract</h2>

This document collects the 979 declarations of the ℤ/9 vortex framework that the Lean 4 kernel accepts — 777 of them THEOREMS closing by exhaustion, 187 PROVED for every value, and 15 rfl declarations shown and marked as such, across 44 source files. Each is stated exactly as the kernel received it, followed by the tactic that discharged it and, for an exhaustion, the size of the finite domain it walked. Every exhaustion is decidable and was checked sorry-free and axiom-free; every proof carries only the standard axioms propext and Quot.sound, printed per file. A content-address proves integrity, not truth: it fixes which statement was checked, not that the statement is significant. <h2 class="paper-h">The size of what was checked</h2>

The domains sum to 156,871,722,610 cases, and that total should not be read as the weight of this work: **one theorem carries 97.257% of it**. The median theorem walks **7** cases, and **306** of 979 walk a single point — a check by evaluation, not by exhaustion. The honest summary is a distribution, not a sum, so it is drawn below rather than reported as one number.

<h2 class="paper-h">Method</h2>

Each theorem is a proposition over a finite domain, discharged by exhaustion: the kernel evaluates the proposition at every point of that domain rather than accepting an argument about it. **777** of 979 are closed by `by decide` and are sealed in the append-only ledger. **187** are PROVED for every value — a proof, not an exhaustion, resting on the standard axioms that core Lean's lemmas carry — and are sealed as proofs, never as decisions. The remaining **15** are settled by `rfl` — a declaration that unfolds to itself — and are deliberately **not sealed**: they are shown here, and marked, because a definitional unfolding is not an exhaustion and must not be counted as one. This is a stronger check than a passing test, and a weaker claim than a proof about the infinite objects the Millennium Problems concern. No Mathlib, no `native_decide`, no `sorry`.

<h2 class="paper-h">How to read this document</h2>

Sections are the Lean source files, ordered by the wing each declares in its own frontmatter; the prose under a section heading is that file's own header comment, and the remark under a theorem is the comment written above it in the source. Nothing here is authored: it is read out of `src/proof/` on every build, so the paper cannot drift from the proofs it describes — a statement that differs from its source stops the build. A remark under a theorem is printed only when the source comment is that theorem's own: **607** of 979 have one. A comment that belongs to the enclosing section is not repeated under each theorem it precedes, because it is context for the section and not a statement about any one of them. Integrity, not truth.

<h2 class="paper-h paper-wing">the address</h2>


### Addressing {#address}

<p class="paper-src"><code>src/proof/address.lean</code> · namespace <code>Address</code> · 26 theorems</p>

The content-address itself, ported to Lean — toUuid, merge, the fold, and their properties.


Everything this deposit calls a receipt is toUuid(seed): four seeded FNV-1a passes, assembled into sixteen
bytes, with the version and variant nibbles forced. Until now those bytes existed only in TypeScript, and
every property the ledger claimed of them — determinism, distinctness, the order-independence of the fold —
was asserted by a test that ran once. Here they are propositions the kernel checks.

A uuid is carried as its SIXTEEN BYTES, which is what it is; the dashed hex string is presentation and
proves nothing extra. Bitwise AND and OR are built structurally for the same reason XOR was: Nat's own
bitwise operations are well-founded and drag `propext` into anything that touches them.

<p class="paper-h">Definitions</p>

<pre class="thm-statement paper-defs"><code>SEEDS := [0, 2654435769, 608135816, 3084996962]
A := [97]                                    -- "a"
UUIDNA := [117, 117, 105, 100, 110, 97]      -- "uuidna"
settledHere := 20</code></pre>

<div class="thm" id="thm-address-distinct_seeds_give_distinct_addresses">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 9</strong> (<code>distinct_seeds_give_distinct_addresses</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_address_distinct_seeds_give_distinct_addresses">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>UUIDNA</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>toUuidBytes A ≠ toUuidBytes UUIDNA</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left(A\right) \neq \mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{UUIDNA}\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-address-addressing_is_injective_on_single_characters">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 10</strong> (<code>addressing_is_injective_on_single_characters</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_address_addressing_is_injective_on_single_characters">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>dedup</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>23</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(((List.range 24).map (fun c =&gt; toUuidBytes [c])).eraseDups).length = 24</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\operatorname{dedup}\left(\{\, \mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([c]\right) \mid c \in \{0,\dots,23\} \,\}\right)\right| = 24</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 24 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-address-addressing_is_not_the_identity">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 11</strong> (<code>addressing_is_not_the_identity</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_address_addressing_is_not_the_identity">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>toUuidBytes [7] ≠ [7]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([7]\right) \neq [7]</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the address is NOT the input: it is not the identity, and it is not constant ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-address-addressing_is_not_constant">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 12</strong> (<code>addressing_is_not_constant</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_address_addressing_is_not_constant">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>toUuidBytes [1] ≠ toUuidBytes [2]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([1]\right) \neq \mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([2]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-address-the_four_seeds_are_distinct">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 13</strong> (<code>the_four_seeds_are_distinct</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_address_the_four_seeds_are_distinct">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>SEEDS.eraseDups</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(SEEDS.eraseDups).length = 4</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\mathrm{SEEDS.eraseDups}\right| = 4</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the four seeds genuinely differ, so the four words are independent draws ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-address-address_settles_its_range">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 14</strong> (<code>address_settles_its_range</code>)<span class="thm-uncited">not sealed — settled by <code>rfl</code>, not exhausted</span>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>settledHere</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>settledHere = 20</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{settledHere} = 20</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>rfl</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-address-the_address_is_sixteen_bytes_whatever_the_input_length">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 15</strong> (<code>the_address_is_sixteen_bytes_whatever_the_input_length</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_address_the_address_is_sixteen_bytes_whatever_the_input_length">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>98</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>117</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>117</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>105</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>110</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>104</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>32</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>109</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>32</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>102</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>112</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>105</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>104</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>117</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>109</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>110</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>105</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>121</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(toUuidBytes [97]).length = 16 ∧ (toUuidBytes [98]).length = 16 ∧ (toUuidBytes [117, 117, 105, 100, 110, 97]).length = 16 ∧ (toUuidBytes [116, 104, 101, 32, 115, 97, 109, 101, 32, 102, 97, 99, 116]).length = 16 ∧ (toUuidBytes [120]).length = 16 ∧ (toUuidBytes [100, 101, 112, 111, 115, 105, 116]).length = 16 ∧ (toUuidBytes [104, 117, 109, 97, 110, 105, 116, 121]).length = 16</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([97]\right)\right| = 16 \land \left|\mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([98]\right)\right| = 16 \land \left|\mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([117,\,117,\,105,\,100,\,110,\,97]\right)\right| = 16 \land \left|\mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([116,\,104,\,101,\,32,\,115,\,97,\,109,\,101,\,32,\,102,\,97,\,99,\,116]\right)\right| = 16 \land \left|\mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([120]\right)\right| = 16 \land \left|\mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([100,\,101,\,112,\,111,\,115,\,105,\,116]\right)\right| = 16 \land \left|\mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([104,\,117,\,109,\,97,\,110,\,105,\,116,\,121]\right)\right| = 16</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">inputs of length 1 to 13 all give 16 bytes — a length-preserving function fails this</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 4,368 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-address-distinct_inputs_give_distinct_addresses">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 16</strong> (<code>distinct_inputs_give_distinct_addresses</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_address_distinct_inputs_give_distinct_addresses">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>98</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>117</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>117</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>105</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>110</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>112</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>105</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>104</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>117</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>109</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>110</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>105</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>121</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>toUuidBytes [97] ≠ toUuidBytes [98] ∧ toUuidBytes [117, 117, 105, 100, 110, 97] ≠ toUuidBytes [120] ∧ toUuidBytes [100, 101, 112, 111, 115, 105, 116] ≠ toUuidBytes [104, 117, 109, 97, 110, 105, 116, 121]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([97]\right) \neq \mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([98]\right) \land \mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([117,\,117,\,105,\,100,\,110,\,97]\right) \neq \mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([120]\right) \land \mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([100,\,101,\,112,\,111,\,115,\,105,\,116]\right) \neq \mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([104,\,117,\,109,\,97,\,110,\,105,\,116,\,121]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">a constant function makes all of these EQUAL, so it fails every conjunct</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 336 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-address-the_address_is_not_the_payload">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 17</strong> (<code>the_address_is_not_the_payload</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_address_the_address_is_not_the_payload">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>117</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>117</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>105</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>110</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>117</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>117</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>105</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>110</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>toUuidBytes [97] ≠ [97] ∧ toUuidBytes [117, 117, 105, 100, 110, 97] ≠ [117, 117, 105, 100, 110, 97]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([97]\right) \neq [97] \land \mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([117,\,117,\,105,\,100,\,110,\,97]\right) \neq [117,\,117,\,105,\,100,\,110,\,97]</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the identity function fails this — the output would BE the input</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 36 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-address-the_address_is_order_sensitive">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 18</strong> (<code>the_address_is_order_sensitive</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_address_the_address_is_order_sensitive">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>98</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>98</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>toUuidBytes [97, 98] ≠ toUuidBytes [98, 97]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([97,\,98]\right) \neq \mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([98,\,97]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">any function of the multiset alone makes these equal</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 4 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-address-the_version_stamp_keeps_the_low_nibble_of_every_byte">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 19</strong> (<code>the_version_stamp_keeps_the_low_nibble_of_every_byte</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_address_the_version_stamp_keeps_the_low_nibble_of_every_byte">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ b : Nat, b &lt; 256 → or8 (and8 b 15) 128 = 128 + b % 16</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the stamp's fields, for every byte ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 128 bits − 4 (version) − 2 (variant) = 122 hash bits. Byte 6 keeps its low nibble under the version 8, byte 8 keeps its low six bits under the variant 10, stamping twice is stamping once, and so the third group is always version 8 over exactly twelve hash bits and the fourth is always variant 10 over exactly fourteen. The address is a commitment to its content, not a store of it: 122 bits is also all a 122-qubit register could yield (Holevo).</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-address-the_variant_stamp_keeps_the_low_six_bits_of_every_byte">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 20</strong> (<code>the_variant_stamp_keeps_the_low_six_bits_of_every_byte</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_address_the_variant_stamp_keeps_the_low_six_bits_of_every_byte">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ b : Nat, b &lt; 256 → or8 (and8 b 63) 128 = 128 + b % 64</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-address-stamping_twice_is_stamping_once">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 21</strong> (<code>stamping_twice_is_stamping_once</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_address_stamping_twice_is_stamping_once">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ b : Nat, b &lt; 256 → or8 (and8 (or8 (and8 b 15) 128) 15) 128 = or8 (and8 b 15) 128 ∧ or8 (and8 (or8 (and8 b 63) 128) 63) 128 = or8 (and8 b 63) 128</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-address-the_third_group_is_version_eight_over_twelve_hash_bits">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 22</strong> (<code>the_third_group_is_version_eight_over_twelve_hash_bits</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_address_the_third_group_is_version_eight_over_twelve_hash_bits">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ b6 b7 : Nat, b6 &lt; 256 → b7 &lt; 256 → (or8 (and8 b6 15) 128) * 256 + b7 = 8 * 4096 + (b6 % 16 * 256 + b7) ∧ b6 % 16 * 256 + b7 &lt; 4096</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-address-the_fourth_group_is_variant_two_over_fourteen_hash_bits">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 23</strong> (<code>the_fourth_group_is_variant_two_over_fourteen_hash_bits</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_address_the_fourth_group_is_variant_two_over_fourteen_hash_bits">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ b8 b9 : Nat, b8 &lt; 256 → b9 &lt; 256 → (or8 (and8 b8 63) 128) * 256 + b9 = 2 * 16384 + (b8 % 64 * 256 + b9) ∧ b8 % 64 * 256 + b9 &lt; 16384</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-address-the_unstamped_bits_read_back_from_every_stamped_byte">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 24</strong> (<code>the_unstamped_bits_read_back_from_every_stamped_byte</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_address_the_unstamped_bits_read_back_from_every_stamped_byte">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ b : Nat, b &lt; 256 → and8 (or8 (and8 b 15) 128) 15 = b % 16 ∧ and8 (or8 (and8 b 63) 128) 63 = b % 64</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── reflections, from the xor batch: each law beside its inverse (the 2×7 ↔ 1+6 wave) ── REFLECTIONS: the unstamped bits read back from the stamped byte, and the hash bits from the group</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-address-the_twelve_hash_bits_read_back_from_the_third_group">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 25</strong> (<code>the_twelve_hash_bits_read_back_from_the_third_group</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_address_the_twelve_hash_bits_read_back_from_the_third_group">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ b6 b7 : Nat, b6 &lt; 256 → b7 &lt; 256 → ((or8 (and8 b6 15) 128) * 256 + b7) / 4096 = 8 ∧ ((or8 (and8 b6 15) 128) * 256 + b7) % 4096 = b6 % 16 * 256 + b7</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-address-the_fourteen_hash_bits_read_back_from_the_fourth_group">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 26</strong> (<code>the_fourteen_hash_bits_read_back_from_the_fourth_group</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_address_the_fourteen_hash_bits_read_back_from_the_fourth_group">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ b8 b9 : Nat, b8 &lt; 256 → b9 &lt; 256 → ((or8 (and8 b8 63) 128) * 256 + b9) / 16384 = 2 ∧ ((or8 (and8 b8 63) 128) * 256 + b9) % 16384 = b8 % 64 * 256 + b9</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>


### What a signature is for, and where it cannot go {#asymmetric}

<p class="paper-src"><code>src/proof/asymmetric.lean</code> · namespace <code>Asymmetric</code> · 12 theorems</p>

2011; standardised as RFC 8032 (Josefsson and Liusvaara, 2017). SHA-512 is FIPS 180-4 (NIST). The
  curve, the signature scheme and the hash are all theirs and none is this deposit's. The implementation
  in src/0/ed25519.ts is checked against their published vectors by scripts/crypto-kat.ts, which is where
  the assurance for the PRIMITIVE lives — not here. Nothing below decides that Ed25519 is secure, and a
  file that appeared to would be claiming a result nobody has.


WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR. Everything cryptographic in this deposit before now was SYMMETRIC — FNV, SHA-256,
HMAC, ChaCha20-Poly1305 — and a symmetric tag proves possession of a shared secret. It cannot say WHO
produced something, because both parties can produce it. That is a boundary the deposit kept in prose.

Two facts are decidable, and they are the two that keep the container honest:

  1 · A CHECKSUM IS NOT AUTHENTICATION. The container's first group holds 32 bits computed by a public
      function of the payload, so anyone who edits the payload recomputes it. Deciding this needs no
      cryptography at all — it is a counting statement about what a public function can distinguish.

  2 · THE SIGNATURE DOES NOT FIT. An Ed25519 public key is 32 bytes and a signature is 64. A uuid is 16
      bytes in total, of which 6 BITS are already spoken for. So a signature is carried beside the
      identifier, never inside it, and "the signature is in the uuid" is arithmetic, not policy.

No axioms, no Mathlib, no sorry.

<p class="paper-h">Definitions</p>

<pre class="thm-statement paper-defs"><code>uuidBytes := 16
publicKeyBytes := 32
signatureBytes := 64
checkBits := 32
payloadBits := 42 + 48
p := 2 ^ 255 - 19
L := 2 ^ 252 + 27742317777372353535851937790883648493
settledHere := 11</code></pre>

<div class="thm" id="thm-asymmetric-a_signature_is_four_uuids_and_a_key_is_two">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 27</strong> (<code>a_signature_is_four_uuids_and_a_key_is_two</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_asymmetric_a_signature_is_four_uuids_and_a_key_is_two">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>signatureBytes</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>uuidBytes</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mi>publicKeyBytes</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>uuidBytes</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>signatureBytes = 4 * uuidBytes ∧ publicKeyBytes = 2 * uuidBytes</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{signatureBytes} = 4 \cdot \mathrm{uuidBytes} \land \mathrm{publicKeyBytes} = 2 \cdot \mathrm{uuidBytes}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-asymmetric-neither_the_key_nor_the_signature_fits_in_a_uuid">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 28</strong> (<code>neither_the_key_nor_the_signature_fits_in_a_uuid</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_asymmetric_neither_the_key_nor_the_signature_fits_in_a_uuid">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>uuidBytes</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>publicKeyBytes</mi></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mi>uuidBytes</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>signatureBytes</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>uuidBytes</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>signatureBytes</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>uuidBytes &lt; publicKeyBytes ∧ uuidBytes &lt; signatureBytes ∧ uuidBytes * 8 &lt; signatureBytes * 8</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{uuidBytes} &lt; \mathrm{publicKeyBytes} \land \mathrm{uuidBytes} &lt; \mathrm{signatureBytes} \land \mathrm{uuidBytes} \cdot 8 &lt; \mathrm{signatureBytes} \cdot 8</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-asymmetric-not_even_the_whole_uuid_would_hold_one">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 29</strong> (<code>not_even_the_whole_uuid_would_hold_one</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_asymmetric_not_even_the_whole_uuid_would_hold_one">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>uuidBytes</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>signatureBytes</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mn>128</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>uuidBytes * 8 = 128 ∧ signatureBytes * 8 = 512 ∧ 128 &lt; 512</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{uuidBytes} \cdot 8 = 128 \land \mathrm{signatureBytes} \cdot 8 = 512 \land 128 &lt; 512</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">and not even if the whole identifier were given over to it, reserved bits and all</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-asymmetric-what_travels_beside_the_identifier">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 30</strong> (<code>what_travels_beside_the_identifier</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_asymmetric_what_travels_beside_the_identifier">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>publicKeyBytes</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>signatureBytes</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>96</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mn>96</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>uuidBytes</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>publicKeyBytes + signatureBytes = 96 ∧ 96 = 6 * uuidBytes</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{publicKeyBytes} + \mathrm{signatureBytes} = 96 \land 96 = 6 \cdot \mathrm{uuidBytes}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the pair travels together, and together they are six times the thing they attest</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-asymmetric-the_check_cannot_separate_the_payloads">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 31</strong> (<code>the_check_cannot_separate_the_payloads</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_asymmetric_the_check_cannot_separate_the_payloads">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>checkBits</mi></msup><mo>&lt;</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>payloadBits</mi></msup></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mi>payloadBits</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>90</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mi>checkBits</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>2 ^ checkBits &lt; 2 ^ payloadBits ∧ payloadBits = 90 ∧ checkBits = 32</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>2^{\mathrm{checkBits}} &lt; 2^{\mathrm{payloadBits}} \land \mathrm{payloadBits} = 90 \land \mathrm{checkBits} = 32</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── A CHECKSUM CANNOT AUTHENTICATE, AND THIS IS COUNTING, NOT CRYPTOGRAPHY ─────────────────────────────── 90 bits of payload cannot be separated by 32 bits of check, so distinct payloads share a check by the pigeonhole alone — before any question of how good the function is.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-asymmetric-the_gap_is_fifty_eight_bits">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 32</strong> (<code>the_gap_is_fifty_eight_bits</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_asymmetric_the_gap_is_fifty_eight_bits">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>payloadBits</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>checkBits</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>58</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>payloadBits</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>58</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>checkBits</mi></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>payloadBits - checkBits = 58 ∧ 2 ^ payloadBits = 2 ^ 58 * 2 ^ checkBits</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{payloadBits} - \mathrm{checkBits} = 58 \land 2^{\mathrm{payloadBits}} = 2^{58} \cdot 2^{\mathrm{checkBits}}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the gap is not marginal: there are 2^58 payloads per check value on average</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-asymmetric-a_checksum_is_the_same_whoever_computes_it">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 33</strong> (<code>a_checksum_is_the_same_whoever_computes_it</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_asymmetric_a_checksum_is_the_same_whoever_computes_it">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>checkOf</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>checkOf</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 6).all (fun s =&gt; (List.range 6).all (fun t =&gt; (List.range 12).all (fun p =&gt; checkOf s p == checkOf t p)))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall s \in \{0,\dots,5\},\; \forall t \in \{0,\dots,5\},\; \forall p \in \{0,\dots,11\},\; \mathrm{checkOf}\mathopen{}\left(s,\,p\right) = \mathrm{checkOf}\mathopen{}\left(t,\,p\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">A CHECKSUM IGNORES THE SECRET: every party computes the same value for the same payload, so it names nobody. Over every pair of secrets and every payload in range.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 432 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-asymmetric-two_secrets_part_company_on_every_payload">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 34</strong> (<code>two_secrets_part_company_on_every_payload</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_asymmetric_two_secrets_part_company_on_every_payload">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>tagOf</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>tagOf</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>tagOf</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>tagOf</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 12).all (fun p =&gt; tagOf 1 p != tagOf 2 p) ∧ ¬ ((List.range 6).all (fun s =&gt; (List.range 6).all (fun t =&gt; (List.range 12).all (fun p =&gt; tagOf s p == tagOf t p))))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall p \in \{0,\dots,11\},\; \mathrm{tagOf}\mathopen{}\left(1,\,p\right) \neq \mathrm{tagOf}\mathopen{}\left(2,\,p\right) \land \lnot \forall s \in \{0,\dots,5\},\; \forall t \in \{0,\dots,5\},\; \forall p \in \{0,\dots,11\},\; \mathrm{tagOf}\mathopen{}\left(s,\,p\right) = \mathrm{tagOf}\mathopen{}\left(t,\,p\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">A TAG DOES NOT: distinct secrets give distinct tags on every payload, which is what lets a verifier tell two parties apart. The identical quantification, and it comes out the other way.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 5,184 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-asymmetric-the_tag_moves_with_the_payload">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 35</strong> (<code>the_tag_moves_with_the_payload</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_asymmetric_the_tag_moves_with_the_payload">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>tagOf</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>tagOf</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 11).all (fun p =&gt; tagOf 1 p != tagOf 1 (p + 1))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall p \in \{0,\dots,10\},\; \mathrm{tagOf}\mathopen{}\left(1,\,p\right) \neq \mathrm{tagOf}\mathopen{}\left(1,\,p + 1\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">and the tag really does depend on the payload too, or it would name the party and attest nothing</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 11 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-asymmetric-the_square_root_rule_is_the_one_this_prime_admits">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 36</strong> (<code>the_square_root_rule_is_the_one_this_prime_admits</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_asymmetric_the_square_root_rule_is_the_one_this_prime_admits">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>p % 8 = 5 ∧ (p + 3) % 8 = 0 ∧ p % 4 = 1 ∧ p % 4 ≠ 3</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>p \bmod 8 = 5 \land p + 3 \bmod 8 = 0 \land p \bmod 4 = 1 \land p \bmod 4 \neq 3</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-asymmetric-the_cofactor_is_bracketed_at_eight">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 37</strong> (<code>the_cofactor_is_bracketed_at_eight</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_asymmetric_the_cofactor_is_bracketed_at_eight">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>4 * L &lt; p ∧ p &lt; 8 * L ∧ L &lt; p</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>4 \cdot L &lt; p \land p &lt; 8 \cdot L \land L &lt; p</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">and the base point's order is the prime part of a group whose cofactor is eight — bracketed, so the 8 is pinned by two inequalities rather than restated as a number somebody could edit to anything</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-asymmetric-asymmetric_settles_its_range">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 38</strong> (<code>asymmetric_settles_its_range</code>)<span class="thm-uncited">not sealed — settled by <code>rfl</code>, not exhausted</span>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>settledHere</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>settledHere = 11</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{settledHere} = 11</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>rfl</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>


### FNV-1a, the address function {#fnv}

<p class="paper-src"><code>src/proof/fnv.lean</code> · namespace <code>Fnv</code> · 15 theorems</p>

FNV-1a, ported to Lean — the hash the whole deposit's addressing rests on.


Every content-address in this deposit is toUuid(seed), and toUuid is four FNV-1a passes over the seed. The
ledger asserted properties of that function in TypeScript — determinism, injectivity on distinct inputs,
order-independence of the fold — and a TypeScript test is a run, not a proof. Porting the hash makes those
properties statable, and `decide` then settles them over whatever finite domain is named.

Two primitives had to be built rather than borrowed. Nat's bitwise operations (`^^^`, `&gt;&gt;&gt;`) and `Nat.gcd`
are defined by well-founded recursion, and their equation lemmas pull `propext` into every theorem that
touches them — a hazard that silently cost two theorems in an earlier batch here. So XOR is a fuel-bounded
structural fold, and the shift is division by a power of two. No axioms, no Mathlib, no sorry.

<p class="paper-h">Definitions</p>

<pre class="thm-statement paper-defs"><code>M32 := 4294967296
FNV_OFFSET := 2166136261   -- 0x811c9dc5
FNV_PRIME := 16777619     -- 0x01000193
MIX1 := 2246822507         -- 0x85ebca6b
MIX2 := 3266489909         -- 0xc2b2ae35
settledHere := 12</code></pre>

<div class="thm" id="thm-fnv-hash_a_seed_zero">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 39</strong> (<code>hash_a_seed_zero</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_fnv_hash_a_seed_zero">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>hash32</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1484191995</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>hash32 0 [97] = 1484191995</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{hash32}\mathopen{}\left(0,\,[97]\right) = 1484191995</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── AGREEMENT with the shipped implementation, at published values ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>hash32</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>117</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>117</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>105</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>110</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>4233172274</mn></mrow></math></div>
