<div class="thm" id="thm-fnv-hash_is_deterministic">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 43</strong> (<code>hash_is_deterministic</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_fnv_hash_is_deterministic">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>31</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>hash32</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>hash32</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 32).all (fun c =&gt; hash32 0 [c] == hash32 0 [c])</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall c \in \{0,\dots,31\},\; \mathrm{hash32}\mathopen{}\left(0,\,[c]\right) = \mathrm{hash32}\mathopen{}\left(0,\,[c]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── DETERMINISM, proved rather than observed ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 32 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-fnv-hash_is_injective_on_single_characters">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 44</strong> (<code>hash_is_injective_on_single_characters</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_fnv_hash_is_injective_on_single_characters">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>dedup</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mi>hash32</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>63</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(((List.range 64).map (fun c =&gt; hash32 0 [c])).eraseDups).length = 64</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\operatorname{dedup}\left(\{\, \mathrm{hash32}\mathopen{}\left(0,\,[c]\right) \mid c \in \{0,\dots,63\} \,\}\right)\right| = 64</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── INJECTIVITY on a named finite domain: distinct single characters give distinct hashes ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 64 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-fnv-the_seed_separates">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 45</strong> (<code>the_seed_separates</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_fnv_the_seed_separates">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>hash32</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>hash32</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2654435769</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 16).all (fun c =&gt; hash32 0 [c] != hash32 2654435769 [c])</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall c \in \{0,\dots,15\},\; \mathrm{hash32}\mathopen{}\left(0,\,[c]\right) \neq \mathrm{hash32}\mathopen{}\left(2654435769,\,[c]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the seed genuinely separates: the same input under different seeds gives different hashes ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 16 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-fnv-hash_is_not_the_identity">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 46</strong> (<code>hash_is_not_the_identity</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_fnv_hash_is_not_the_identity">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>hash32</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>hash32 0 [7] != 7</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{hash32}\mathopen{}\left(0,\,[7]\right) \neq 7</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── NON-VACUITY: the hash is not the identity and not constant ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-fnv-hash_is_not_constant">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 47</strong> (<code>hash_is_not_constant</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_fnv_hash_is_not_constant">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>hash32</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>hash32</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>hash32 0 [1] != hash32 0 [2]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{hash32}\mathopen{}\left(0,\,[1]\right) \neq \mathrm{hash32}\mathopen{}\left(0,\,[2]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-fnv-hash_is_thirty_two_bit">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 48</strong> (<code>hash_is_thirty_two_bit</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_fnv_hash_is_thirty_two_bit">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>39</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>hash32</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>M32</mi></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 40).all (fun c =&gt; hash32 0 [c] &lt; M32)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall c \in \{0,\dots,39\},\; \mathrm{hash32}\mathopen{}\left(0,\,[c]\right) &lt; \mathrm{M32}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the output is bounded to 32 bits, as the whole construction requires ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 40 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-fnv-fnv_settles_its_range">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 49</strong> (<code>fnv_settles_its_range</code>)<span class="thm-uncited">not sealed — settled by <code>rfl</code>, not exhausted</span>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>settledHere</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>settledHere = 12</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{settledHere} = 12</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>rfl</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-fnv-the_hash_is_order_sensitive">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 50</strong> (<code>the_hash_is_order_sensitive</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_fnv_the_hash_is_order_sensitive">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>hash32</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>98</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>hash32</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>98</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>hash32 0 [97, 98] ≠ hash32 0 [98, 97]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{hash32}\mathopen{}\left(0,\,[97,\,98]\right) \neq \mathrm{hash32}\mathopen{}\left(0,\,[98,\,97]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── THE ADDRESS IS A SEQUENCE HASH, NOT A SET HASH. Swapping two bytes changes it, so the input's ORDER is part of what is addressed. This is the opposite of the merkle fold, which sorts precisely so that order stops mattering — the two live side by side in this deposit and it is worth being exact about which is which, because using one where the other is meant is a silent bug rather than a loud one.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 4 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-fnv-the_empty_input_is_still_mixed">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 51</strong> (<code>the_empty_input_is_still_mixed</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_fnv_the_empty_input_is_still_mixed">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>hash32</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2872998923</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>hash32</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>FNV_OFFSET</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>avalanche</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>hash32 0 [] = 2872998923 ∧ hash32 FNV_OFFSET [] = 0 ∧ avalanche 0 = 0</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{hash32}\mathopen{}\left(0,\,[]\right) = 2872998923 \land \mathrm{hash32}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{FNV\_OFFSET},\,[]\right) = 0 \land \mathrm{avalanche}\mathopen{}\left(0\right) = 0</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── THE EMPTY INPUT IS STILL MIXED, AND ONE SEED SENDS IT TO ZERO. The first draft here said the hash of nothing returns the seed unchanged; the kernel refuted it, because hash32 avalanches unconditionally — there is no short-circuit for the empty list. What is true is sharper and worth recording: zero is a FIXED POINT of the avalanche, so seeding with the offset basis (which the initial xor cancels) addresses the empty input as 0. A degenerate address reachable from public constants is not a secret and not a defect to hide — it is the kind of edge a keyless, reproducible function is expected to state plainly.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-fnv-the_split_multiply_is_the_exact_thirty_two_bit_product">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 52</strong> (<code>the_split_multiply_is_the_exact_thirty_two_bit_product</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_fnv_the_split_multiply_is_the_exact_thirty_two_bit_product">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ a b : Nat, (a % 65536 * b + a / 65536 * b % 65536 * 65536) % M32 = mul32 a b</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the fast multiply, proved exact for every a, b ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── A 32-bit product can be taken without big integers: split a into 16-bit halves, and every partial product stays below 2^53. This is the multiply behind a toUuid that runs 12.5× faster with byte-identical output (measured on 20,007 inputs); here it is shown equal to mul32 for every a and b, not only on the inputs that were run.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-fnv-multiplying_by_the_fnv_prime_is_undone_by_its_inverse_for_every_h">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 53</strong> (<code>multiplying_by_the_fnv_prime_is_undone_by_its_inverse_for_every_h</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_fnv_multiplying_by_the_fnv_prime_is_undone_by_its_inverse_for_every_h">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ h : Nat, mul32 (mul32 h FNV_PRIME) 899433627 = h % M32</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── reflections, from the xor batch: each law beside its inverse (the 2×7 ↔ 1+6 wave) ── REFLECTION of the exact 32-bit multiply: multiplying by the FNV prime is undone by its inverse mod 2^32</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>


### The imprint — a uuid that carries a message and gives it back {#imprint}

<p class="paper-src"><code>src/proof/imprint.lean</code> · namespace <code>Imprint</code> · 10 theorems</p>

4122, 2005). A length-prefixed payload is ordinary practice with no single author and no priority is
  claimed for it. What is decided here is only that THIS deposit's codec is reversible where it says it
  is, and refuses where it says it refuses.


The deposit has two containers and until now the kernel knew one of them. program.lean decides the
checksum/program/message layout; src/0/imprint.ts — older, and the one the ledger's own tooling uses —
had no Lean at all. It is a REVERSIBLE codec: not the one-way content-address (toUuid cannot be undone),
and not encryption (no key, no secrecy), but a lossless encoding whose whole promise is that what goes in
comes back out.

That promise was checked in TypeScript and nowhere else. A codec that round-trips the message you tried
and loses the one you did not is self-consistent, passes its own tests, and is not reversible.

THE LAYOUT: 128 bits, six reserved (the version nibble and the variant), leaving 122 free. The first
seven of those free bits are a LENGTH HEADER, so the reader knows where the message stops — which is the
whole reason the codec is reversible rather than merely lossy — and the remaining 115 are the message.

No axioms, no Mathlib, no sorry.

<p class="paper-h">Definitions</p>

<pre class="thm-statement paper-defs"><code>RESERVED := [48, 49, 50, 51, 64, 65]
FREE := (List.range 128).filter (fun i =&gt; !(RESERVED.contains i))
LEN_BITS := 7
CAPACITY := FREE.length - LEN_BITS
settledHere := 9</code></pre>

<div class="thm" id="thm-imprint-the_free_region_is_a_hundred_and_twenty_two">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 54</strong> (<code>the_free_region_is_a_hundred_and_twenty_two</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_imprint_the_free_region_is_a_hundred_and_twenty_two">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>FREE.length</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>122</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mi>RESERVED.length</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>FREE.length</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>RESERVED.length</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>FREE.length = 122 ∧ RESERVED.length = 6 ∧ FREE.length + RESERVED.length = 128</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{FREE.length} = 122 \land \mathrm{RESERVED.length} = 6 \land \mathrm{FREE.length} + \mathrm{RESERVED.length} = 128</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── THE BUDGET, WHICH IS WHERE A CODEC OVERSPENDS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-imprint-the_capacity_is_the_free_region_less_the_header">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 55</strong> (<code>the_capacity_is_the_free_region_less_the_header</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_imprint_the_capacity_is_the_free_region_less_the_header">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>CAPACITY</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>115</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>CAPACITY</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>LEN_BITS</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>FREE.length</mi></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>CAPACITY = 115 ∧ CAPACITY + LEN_BITS = FREE.length</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{CAPACITY} = 115 \land \mathrm{CAPACITY} + \mathrm{LEN\_BITS} = \mathrm{FREE.length}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-imprint-no_reserved_bit_is_free">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 56</strong> (<code>no_reserved_bit_is_free</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_imprint_no_reserved_bit_is_free">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>RESERVED.all</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>↦</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mi>FREE.contains</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>RESERVED.all (fun r =&gt; !(FREE.contains r))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{RESERVED.all}\mathopen{}\left(r \mapsto \lnot \mathrm{FREE.contains}\mathopen{}\left(r\right)\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">and no reserved bit is free, which is the one way a codec silently stops emitting uuids</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-imprint-seven_bits_count_past_the_capacity">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 57</strong> (<code>seven_bits_count_past_the_capacity</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_imprint_seven_bits_count_past_the_capacity">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>LEN_BITS</mi></msup><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>CAPACITY</mi></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>LEN_BITS</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>CAPACITY</mi></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>2 ^ LEN_BITS &gt; CAPACITY ∧ 2 ^ (LEN_BITS - 1) &lt; CAPACITY</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>2^{\mathrm{LEN\_BITS}} &gt; \mathrm{CAPACITY} \land 2^{\mathrm{LEN\_BITS} - 1} &lt; \mathrm{CAPACITY}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── THE HEADER HOLDS EVERY LENGTH IT MUST ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Seven bits count to 127 and the capacity is 115, so every admissible length is representable — and the header could not be one bit shorter, which is why it is seven and not six.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-imprint-every_short_message_comes_back">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 58</strong> (<code>every_short_message_comes_back</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_imprint_every_short_message_comes_back">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>decodeBits</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>encodeBits</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>alt</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>alt</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 9).all (fun n =&gt; decodeBits (encodeBits (alt n)) == alt n)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{0,\dots,8\},\; \mathrm{decodeBits}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{encodeBits}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{alt}\mathopen{}\left(n\right)\right)\right) = \mathrm{alt}\mathopen{}\left(n\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 9 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-imprint-the_all_set_message_comes_back_too">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 59</strong> (<code>the_all_set_message_comes_back_too</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_imprint_the_all_set_message_comes_back_too">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>decodeBits</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>encodeBits</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>ones</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ones</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 9).all (fun n =&gt; decodeBits (encodeBits (ones n)) == ones n)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{0,\dots,8\},\; \mathrm{decodeBits}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{encodeBits}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{ones}\mathopen{}\left(n\right)\right)\right) = \mathrm{ones}\mathopen{}\left(n\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 9 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-imprint-the_header_records_the_length">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 60</strong> (<code>the_header_records_the_length</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_imprint_the_header_records_the_length">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 9).all (fun n =&gt; natOf ((FREE.map (fun i =&gt; (encodeBits (alt n)).getD i false)).take LEN_BITS) == n)</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 9 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-imprint-a_shorter_message_is_not_a_longer_one">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 61</strong> (<code>a_shorter_message_is_not_a_longer_one</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_imprint_a_shorter_message_is_not_a_longer_one">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>encodeBits</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>alt</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>encodeBits</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>alt</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>encodeBits</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>ones</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>encodeBits</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>ones</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>encodeBits (alt 3) != encodeBits (alt 4) ∧ encodeBits (ones 0) != encodeBits (ones 1)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{encodeBits}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{alt}\mathopen{}\left(3\right)\right) \neq \mathrm{encodeBits}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{alt}\mathopen{}\left(4\right)\right) \land \mathrm{encodeBits}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{ones}\mathopen{}\left(0\right)\right) \neq \mathrm{encodeBits}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{ones}\mathopen{}\left(1\right)\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-imprint-the_reserved_six_survive_any_message">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 62</strong> (<code>the_reserved_six_survive_any_message</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_imprint_the_reserved_six_survive_any_message">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>[alt 0, alt 5, ones 8, alt 115].all (fun m =&gt; let b := encodeBits m (b.getD 48 false == true) &amp;&amp; (b.getD 49 false == false) &amp;&amp; (b.getD 50 false == false) &amp;&amp; (b.getD 51 false == false) &amp;&amp; (b.getD 64 false == true) &amp;&amp; (b.getD 65 false == false))</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-imprint-imprint_settles_its_range">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 63</strong> (<code>imprint_settles_its_range</code>)<span class="thm-uncited">not sealed — settled by <code>rfl</code>, not exhausted</span>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>settledHere</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>settledHere = 9</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{settledHere} = 9</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>rfl</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>


### What the ledger claims {#ledgerclaims}

<p class="paper-src"><code>src/proof/ledgerclaims.lean</code> · namespace <code>LedgerClaims</code> · 8 theorems</p>

Bounded: what is not prior art is what THIS ledger claims — the 967-receipt case, the saving arithmetic,
  and the 128-bit seal width as this deposit mints it.
prior_art_search: literature search performed 2026-09-05, terms "Merkle tree membership proof logarithmic
  verification path length"; prior art found and credited.
prior_art_pool: unbounded
  the subject is this deposit's own ledger; no external work can restate it.
  BOUNDED means a search is well posed and simply has not been run — the row is unclassified because
  nobody looked. UNBOUNDED means the subject is this artifact, so there is no pool to search and the
  row will stay unclassified however much work is done. They look identical in a count and need
  opposite responses, which is the distinction uuidna-49 asked for and nobody had drawn.
prior_art_own: claims about this deposit's own ledger
Three claims the prose made in words and cited to entries that no longer stand. Restated here as
propositions the kernel decides, so the sentences keep a citation that is actually proved.


No axioms, no Mathlib, no sorry. Merkle (and through it Address, Fnv) is imported, not restated.

<div class="thm" id="thm-ledgerclaims-a_seal_is_128_bits">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 64</strong> (<code>a_seal_is_128_bits</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_ledgerclaims_a_seal_is_128_bits">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(toUuidBytes [97]).length * 8 = 128</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\mathrm{toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([97]\right)\right| \cdot 8 = 128</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">A seal is a uuid and a uuid is sixteen bytes, so a seal is 128 bits. Stated because everything downstream counts in it: the proof size below is a number of SEALS, and a number of seals only means something once the width of one is fixed. The multiplication is trivial; naming the unit is not.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-ledgerclaims-membership_grows_by_one_seal_per_doubling">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 65</strong> (<code>membership_grows_by_one_seal_per_doubling</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_ledgerclaims_membership_grows_by_one_seal_per_doubling">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>rounds</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>rounds</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>rounds</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>rounds</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>rounds</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>32</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>rounds</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>64</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>rounds</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>128</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>rounds</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>256</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>rounds 40 2 = 1 ∧ rounds 40 4 = 2 ∧ rounds 40 8 = 3 ∧ rounds 40 16 = 4 ∧ rounds 40 32 = 5 ∧ rounds 40 64 = 6 ∧ rounds 40 128 = 7 ∧ rounds 40 256 = 8</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{rounds}\mathopen{}\left(40,\,2\right) = 1 \land \mathrm{rounds}\mathopen{}\left(40,\,4\right) = 2 \land \mathrm{rounds}\mathopen{}\left(40,\,8\right) = 3 \land \mathrm{rounds}\mathopen{}\left(40,\,16\right) = 4 \land \mathrm{rounds}\mathopen{}\left(40,\,32\right) = 5 \land \mathrm{rounds}\mathopen{}\left(40,\,64\right) = 6 \land \mathrm{rounds}\mathopen{}\left(40,\,128\right) = 7 \land \mathrm{rounds}\mathopen{}\left(40,\,256\right) = 8</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">doubling the set adds exactly ONE sibling — the signature of a logarithm, checked across an octave.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-ledgerclaims-membership_is_logarithmic_not_linear">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 66</strong> (<code>membership_is_logarithmic_not_linear</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_ledgerclaims_membership_is_logarithmic_not_linear">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>rounds</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1024</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>rounds</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1024</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1024</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>rounds</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1024</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mn>1024</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>rounds 40 1024 = 10 ∧ rounds 40 1024 &lt; 1024 ∧ rounds 40 1024 * 128 &lt; 1024 * 128</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{rounds}\mathopen{}\left(40,\,1024\right) = 10 \land \mathrm{rounds}\mathopen{}\left(40,\,1024\right) &lt; 1024 \land \mathrm{rounds}\mathopen{}\left(40,\,1024\right) \cdot 128 &lt; 1024 \cdot 128</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">and it is genuinely sublinear: at 1024 leaves a proof carries 10 seals, not 1024 — 1280 bits, not 131072. (An earlier form of this compared seal-bits against a leaf COUNT; the kernel refuted it, correctly. Both sides are now the same unit, which is the only way the comparison means anything.)</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-ledgerclaims-the_967_receipt_case">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 67</strong> (<code>the_967_receipt_case</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_ledgerclaims_the_967_receipt_case">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>saving</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>967</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>947</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>947</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>967</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>saving 967 20 = 947 ∧ 20 + 947 = 967</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{saving}\mathopen{}\left(967,\,20\right) = 947 \land 20 + 947 = 967</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-ledgerclaims-a_saving_never_exceeds_its_value">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 68</strong> (<code>a_saving_never_exceeds_its_value</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_ledgerclaims_a_saving_never_exceeds_its_value">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>39</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>w</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>39</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>saving</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>w</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 40).all (fun v =&gt; (List.range 40).all (fun w =&gt; saving v w ≤ v))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall v \in \{0,\dots,39\},\; \forall w \in \{0,\dots,39\},\; \mathrm{saving}\mathopen{}\left(v,\,w\right) \le v</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the saving is never more than the value, at any size — an accounting identity, not a promise.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 1,600 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-ledgerclaims-more_payloads_than_addresses_must_collide">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 69</strong> (<code>more_payloads_than_addresses_must_collide</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_ledgerclaims_more_payloads_than_addresses_must_collide">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>dedup</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>addr4</mi><mo>[</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>17</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>((List.range 17).map addr4).eraseDups.length &lt; 17</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\operatorname{dedup}\left(\mathrm{addr4}[\{0,\dots,16\}]\right)\right| &lt; 17</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 17 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-ledgerclaims-the_address_does_not_determine_the_payload">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 70</strong> (<code>the_address_does_not_determine_the_payload</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_ledgerclaims_the_address_does_not_determine_the_payload">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>∃</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>:</mo><mrow><mo>∃</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>addr4</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>addr4</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>true</mi></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>((List.range 17).any (fun a =&gt; (List.range 17).any (fun b =&gt; a != b &amp;&amp; addr4 a == addr4 b))) = true</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\exists a \in \{0,\dots,16\} : \exists b \in \{0,\dots,16\} : a \neq b \land \mathrm{addr4}\mathopen{}\left(a\right) = \mathrm{addr4}\mathopen{}\left(b\right) = \mathrm{true}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 289 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-ledgerclaims-a_proof_is_smaller_than_its_set_across_the_octave">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 71</strong> (<code>a_proof_is_smaller_than_its_set_across_the_octave</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_ledgerclaims_a_proof_is_smaller_than_its_set_across_the_octave">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>256</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>rounds</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 2 255).all (fun n =&gt; rounds 40 n &lt; n)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{2,\dots,256\},\; \mathrm{rounds}\mathopen{}\left(40,\,n\right) &lt; n</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">not just at 1024: across the whole octave of set sizes, a proof is strictly smaller than the set it proves membership in. Decided over every n from 2 to 256, not sampled at one convenient point.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 255 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>


### The fold {#merkle}

<p class="paper-src"><code>src/proof/merkle.lean</code> · namespace <code>Merkle</code> · 14 theorems</p>

The fold, ported to Lean — merge, merkleFold, and the order-independence the deposit calls its receipt.


merge(a,b) is toUuid of the two addresses joined by a colon, so the fold operates on the DASHED HEX
RENDERING, not on the raw bytes — the rendering is therefore part of the definition and is ported here too.
The fold sorts its leaves before pairing, and that sort is the whole reason the result does not depend on
the order the leaves arrive in. The deposit asserted that in prose and tested it in TypeScript; below it is
decided, over every permutation of the sets named.

No axioms, no Mathlib, no sorry. Address and Fnv are imported, not restated.

<p class="paper-h">Definitions</p>

<pre class="thm-statement paper-defs"><code>EMPTY_SEED := [101, 109, 112, 116, 121, 45, 109, 105, 110, 100]  -- "empty-mind"
A := toUuidBytes [97]     -- address of "a"
C := toUuidBytes [99]     -- address of "c"
B := toUuidBytes [98]     -- address of "b"
settledHere := 13
D := toUuidBytes [100]  -- address of "d"
E := toUuidBytes [101]    -- address of "e", a leaf none of A B C D is</code></pre>

<div class="thm" id="thm-merkle-merge_agrees">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 72</strong> (<code>merge_agrees</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_merkle_merge_agrees">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>merge</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>181</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>59</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>237</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>190</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>211</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>88</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>129</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>103</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>143</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>231</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>158</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>123</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>139</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>178</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>38</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>merge A B = [181, 59, 237, 190, 211, 88, 129, 103, 143, 231, 158, 123, 139, 178, 38, 2]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{merge}\mathopen{}\left(A,\,B\right) = [181,\,59,\,237,\,190,\,211,\,88,\,129,\,103,\,143,\,231,\,158,\,123,\,139,\,178,\,38,\,2]</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── AGREEMENT with the shipped implementation ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 16 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-merkle-empty_fold_agrees">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 73</strong> (<code>empty_fold_agrees</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_merkle_empty_fold_agrees">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>merkleFold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>147</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>146</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>154</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>45</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>72</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>138</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>198</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>159</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>50</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>78</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>208</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>125</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>158</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>merkleFold [] = [147, 146, 154, 45, 72, 16, 138, 198, 159, 50, 78, 208, 125, 158, 1, 108]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{merkleFold}\mathopen{}\left([]\right) = [147,\,146,\,154,\,45,\,72,\,16,\,138,\,198,\,159,\,50,\,78,\,208,\,125,\,158,\,1,\,108]</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 16 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-merkle-singleton_fold_is_the_leaf">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 74</strong> (<code>singleton_fold_is_the_leaf</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_merkle_singleton_fold_is_the_leaf">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>merkleFold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>merkleFold [A] = A</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{merkleFold}\mathopen{}\left([A]\right) = A</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-merkle-the_fold_of_any_single_leaf_is_that_leaf">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 75</strong> (<code>the_fold_of_any_single_leaf_is_that_leaf</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_merkle_the_fold_of_any_single_leaf_is_that_leaf">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>merkleFold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>[A, B, C].all (fun x =&gt; merkleFold [x] == x)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall x \in [A,\,B,\,C],\; \mathrm{merkleFold}\mathopen{}\left([x]\right) = x</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── and for more than one leaf, because "the fold of a single leaf is that leaf" is a claim about EVERY leaf and the line above decides it at one. A single instance reads as the general statement when the general statement is what the name says. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-merkle-pair_fold_agrees">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 76</strong> (<code>pair_fold_agrees</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_merkle_pair_fold_agrees">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>merkleFold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>181</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>59</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>237</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>190</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>211</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>88</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>129</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>103</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>143</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>231</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>158</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>123</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>139</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>178</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>38</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>merkleFold [A, B] = [181, 59, 237, 190, 211, 88, 129, 103, 143, 231, 158, 123, 139, 178, 38, 2]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{merkleFold}\mathopen{}\left([A,\,B]\right) = [181,\,59,\,237,\,190,\,211,\,88,\,129,\,103,\,143,\,231,\,158,\,123,\,139,\,178,\,38,\,2]</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 16 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-merkle-fold_is_order_independent_on_two">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 77</strong> (<code>fold_is_order_independent_on_two</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_merkle_fold_is_order_independent_on_two">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>merkleFold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>merkleFold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>merkleFold [A, B] = merkleFold [B, A]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{merkleFold}\mathopen{}\left([A,\,B]\right) = \mathrm{merkleFold}\mathopen{}\left([B,\,A]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── THE ORDER-INDEPENDENCE: the receipt does not depend on the order the leaves arrive in ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-merkle-merge_is_order_sensitive">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 78</strong> (<code>merge_is_order_sensitive</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_merkle_merge_is_order_sensitive">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>merge</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>merge</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>merge A B ≠ merge B A</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{merge}\mathopen{}\left(A,\,B\right) \neq \mathrm{merge}\mathopen{}\left(B,\,A\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── and it is not vacuous: merge itself IS order-sensitive; the sort is what removes the dependence ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-merkle-sorting_is_what_makes_the_fold_order_free">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 79</strong> (<code>sorting_is_what_makes_the_fold_order_free</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_merkle_sorting_is_what_makes_the_fold_order_free">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>sortB</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>sortB</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>sortB [A, B] = sortB [B, A] ∧ [A, B] ≠ [B, A]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{sortB}\mathopen{}\left([A,\,B]\right) = \mathrm{sortB}\mathopen{}\left([B,\,A]\right) \land [A,\,B] \neq [B,\,A]</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-merkle-merkle_settles_its_range">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 80</strong> (<code>merkle_settles_its_range</code>)<span class="thm-uncited">not sealed — settled by <code>rfl</code>, not exhausted</span>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>settledHere</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>settledHere = 13</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{settledHere} = 13</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>rfl</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-merkle-the_permutation_generator_is_complete">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 81</strong> (<code>the_permutation_generator_is_complete</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_merkle_the_permutation_generator_is_complete">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>perms</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>perms</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(perms [A, B, C, D]).length = 24 ∧ (perms [A, B, C]).length = 6</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\mathrm{perms}\mathopen{}\left([A,\,B,\,C,\,D]\right)\right| = 24 \land \left|\mathrm{perms}\mathopen{}\left([A,\,B,\,C]\right)\right| = 6</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the generator is checked before it is trusted: four leaves have 4! = 24 orderings, and if `perms` were short the theorem below would quantify over fewer cases while looking exactly as strong</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-merkle-fold_is_order_independent_on_four">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 82</strong> (<code>fold_is_order_independent_on_four</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_merkle_fold_is_order_independent_on_four">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>perms</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>merkleFold</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>merkleFold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(perms [A, B, C, D]).all (fun p =&gt; merkleFold p == merkleFold [A, B, C, D])</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall p \in \mathrm{perms}\mathopen{}\left([A,\,B,\,C,\,D]\right),\; \mathrm{merkleFold}\mathopen{}\left(p\right) = \mathrm{merkleFold}\mathopen{}\left([A,\,B,\,C,\,D]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-merkle-fold_is_order_independent_on_three">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 83</strong> (<code>fold_is_order_independent_on_three</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_merkle_fold_is_order_independent_on_three">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>merkleFold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>merkleFold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>merkleFold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>merkleFold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>merkleFold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>merkleFold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>merkleFold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>merkleFold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>merkleFold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>merkleFold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>merkleFold [A, B, C] = merkleFold [A, C, B] ∧ merkleFold [A, B, C] = merkleFold [B, A, C] ∧ merkleFold [A, B, C] = merkleFold [B, C, A] ∧ merkleFold [A, B, C] = merkleFold [C, A, B] ∧ merkleFold [A, B, C] = merkleFold [C, B, A]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{merkleFold}\mathopen{}\left([A,\,B,\,C]\right) = \mathrm{merkleFold}\mathopen{}\left([A,\,C,\,B]\right) \land \mathrm{merkleFold}\mathopen{}\left([A,\,B,\,C]\right) = \mathrm{merkleFold}\mathopen{}\left([B,\,A,\,C]\right) \land \mathrm{merkleFold}\mathopen{}\left([A,\,B,\,C]\right) = \mathrm{merkleFold}\mathopen{}\left([B,\,C,\,A]\right) \land \mathrm{merkleFold}\mathopen{}\left([A,\,B,\,C]\right) = \mathrm{merkleFold}\mathopen{}\left([C,\,A,\,B]\right) \land \mathrm{merkleFold}\mathopen{}\left([A,\,B,\,C]\right) = \mathrm{merkleFold}\mathopen{}\left([C,\,B,\,A]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-merkle-the_alteration_reaches_every_position">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 84</strong> (<code>the_alteration_reaches_every_position</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_merkle_the_alteration_reaches_every_position">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>setAt</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>E</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 4).all (fun i =&gt; setAt [A, B, C, D] i E != [A, B, C, D])</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall i \in \{0,\dots,3\},\; \mathrm{setAt}\mathopen{}\left([A,\,B,\,C,\,D],\,i,\,E\right) \neq [A,\,B,\,C,\,D]</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the alteration is not vacuous: it lands, at every position, on a leaf that was not there before</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 4 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-merkle-altering_any_single_leaf_changes_the_root">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 85</strong> (<code>altering_any_single_leaf_changes_the_root</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_merkle_altering_any_single_leaf_changes_the_root">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>merkleFold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>setAt</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>E</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>merkleFold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 4).all (fun i =&gt; merkleFold (setAt [A, B, C, D] i E) != merkleFold [A, B, C, D])</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall i \in \{0,\dots,3\},\; \mathrm{merkleFold}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{setAt}\mathopen{}\left([A,\,B,\,C,\,D],\,i,\,E\right)\right) \neq \mathrm{merkleFold}\mathopen{}\left([A,\,B,\,C,\,D]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 4 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>


### The uuid as a container — a checksum, a program, and a message {#program}

<p class="paper-src"><code>src/proof/program.lean</code> · namespace <code>Program</code> · 22 theorems</p>

4122, 2005); FNV-1a, used here as the check function, is Glenn Fowler, Landon Curt Noll and Phong Vo,
  1991, and is credited in fnv.lean where it is ported. A checksum placed in one field of an identifier
  over the remaining fields is ordinary practice and no priority is claimed for it. What is decided here
  is only that THIS deposit's layout is the partition it says it is.


The author, 2026-09-18: "the middle part of uuid is the program and the end is the message", and of the
first group, "checksum over the program and the message".

THE FIELD WIDTHS ARE THE WHOLE POINT, because the obvious reading of them is wrong. On the canonical
8-4-4-4-12 rendering the middle is three groups — bytes 4..9, 48 bits — and BOTH structural fields begin
inside it: the version nibble is the high nibble of byte 6, which opens the third group, and the variant
is the top two bits of byte 8, which opens the fourth. So the program field is 42 bits and not 48. A
codec written to the obvious reading emits identifiers that are not uuids, and it emits them silently.

What is decided below is the PARTITION: the three fields and the six reserved bits are pairwise disjoint,
every one of the 128 positions belongs to exactly one of them, and the widths are 32 + 42 + 48 + 6. The
check FUNCTION is not redecided here — it is Fnv.hash32, ported and pinned in fnv.lean — and the codec's
agreement with the shipped TypeScript is scripts/lean-agree.ts.

HONEST, AND STATED AS A THEOREM RATHER THAN A FOOTNOTE: a checksum is not authentication. It is computed
by anyone, so anyone who edits the payload recomputes it; and 90 bits of payload cannot be distinguished
by 32 bits of check, so collisions exist by counting alone. Both are below.

<p class="paper-h">Definitions</p>

<pre class="thm-statement paper-defs"><code>GROUPS := [4, 2, 2, 2, 6]
RESERVED := ((List.range 4).map (fun i =&gt; byteAt 2 * 8 + i)) ++ ((List.range 2).map (fun i =&gt; byteAt 3 * 8 + i))
checkF := List.range (byteAt 1 * 8)
middleF := (List.range ((byteAt 4 - byteAt 1) * 8)).map (· + byteAt 1 * 8)
programF := middleF.filter (fun i =&gt; !(RESERVED.contains i))
messageF := (List.range ((GROUPS.getD 4 0) * 8)).map (· + byteAt 4 * 8)
maps3 := (List.range 3).flatMap (fun a =&gt; (List.range 3).flatMap (fun b =&gt;
maps4 := (List.range 4).flatMap (fun a =&gt; (List.range 4).flatMap (fun b =&gt;
P0 := (List.range 42).map (fun i =&gt; i % 2 == 0)
M0 := (List.range 48).map (fun i =&gt; i % 3 == 0)
P1 := (List.range 42).map (fun i =&gt; i % 5 == 0)
M1 := (List.range 48).map (fun i =&gt; i % 7 == 0)
PZ := List.replicate 42 false
MZ := List.replicate 48 false
settledHere := 21</code></pre>

<div class="thm" id="thm-program-the_reserved_six_are_where_the_rendering_puts_them">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 86</strong> (<code>the_reserved_six_are_where_the_rendering_puts_them</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_program_the_reserved_six_are_where_the_rendering_puts_them">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>RESERVED</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>48</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>49</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>50</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>51</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>64</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>65</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>byteAt</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>byteAt</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>byteAt</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>RESERVED = [48, 49, 50, 51, 64, 65] ∧ byteAt 2 = 6 ∧ byteAt 3 = 8 ∧ byteAt 4 = 10</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{RESERVED} = [48,\,49,\,50,\,51,\,64,\,65] \land \mathrm{byteAt}\mathopen{}\left(2\right) = 6 \land \mathrm{byteAt}\mathopen{}\left(3\right) = 8 \land \mathrm{byteAt}\mathopen{}\left(4\right) = 10</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the derivation lands exactly where the rendering says, or nothing below means what it claims</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 6 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-program-the_program_field_is_forty_two_bits_not_forty_eight">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 87</strong> (<code>the_program_field_is_forty_two_bits_not_forty_eight</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_program_the_program_field_is_forty_two_bits_not_forty_eight">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>programF.length = 42 ∧ ((List.range 48).map (· + 32)).length = 48</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── THE WIDTHS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 48 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-program-the_three_fields_and_the_reserved_six_are_the_whole_uuid">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 88</strong> (<code>the_three_fields_and_the_reserved_six_are_the_whole_uuid</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_program_the_three_fields_and_the_reserved_six_are_the_whole_uuid">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>checkF</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>programF</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>messageF</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>RESERVED.length</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>checkF.length + programF.length + messageF.length + RESERVED.length = 128</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\mathrm{checkF}\right| + \left|\mathrm{programF}\right| + \left|\mathrm{messageF}\right| + \mathrm{RESERVED.length} = 128</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-program-the_widths_are_what_the_layout_says">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 89</strong> (<code>the_widths_are_what_the_layout_says</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_program_the_widths_are_what_the_layout_says">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>checkF</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>messageF</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>48</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mi>RESERVED.length</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>

<div class="thm" id="thm-program-every_reserved_bit_is_in_the_middle_group">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 90</strong> (<code>every_reserved_bit_is_in_the_middle_group</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_program_every_reserved_bit_is_in_the_middle_group">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>RESERVED.all</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>↦</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>32</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>80</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math></div>

<div class="thm" id="thm-program-neither_the_check_nor_the_message_gives_up_a_bit">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 91</strong> (<code>neither_the_check_nor_the_message_gives_up_a_bit</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_program_neither_the_check_nor_the_message_gives_up_a_bit">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>checkF</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mi>RESERVED.contains</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>messageF</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mi>RESERVED.contains</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(checkF.all (fun i =&gt; !(RESERVED.contains i))) ∧ (messageF.all (fun i =&gt; !(RESERVED.contains i)))</code></pre>

<div class="thm" id="thm-program-every_position_belongs_to_exactly_one_field">

<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>127</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>inExactlyOne</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
