<p class="thm-remark">── 1 · THE THREE PLANCK UNITS CARRY ONE RELATIVE UNCERTAINTY ───────────────────────────────────────────── Length, time and mass are three different quantities in three different units, and the width of what is known about them is the same number, because they are built from the same measured constant.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-the_square_root_halves_what_is_known_about_the_measured_constant">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 276</strong> (<code>the_square_root_halves_what_is_known_about_the_measured_constant</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_the_square_root_halves_what_is_known_about_the_measured_constant">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>ppm</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>ellP</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ellPUnc</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ppm</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>bigG</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>bigGUnc</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>ppm</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>tP</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>tPUnc</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ppm</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>bigG</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>bigGUnc</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>ppm</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>mP</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>mPUnc</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ppm</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>bigG</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>bigGUnc</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>2 * ppm ellP ellPUnc = ppm bigG bigGUnc ∧ 2 * ppm tP tPUnc = ppm bigG bigGUnc ∧ 2 * ppm mP mPUnc = ppm bigG bigGUnc</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>2 \cdot \mathrm{ppm}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{ellP},\,\mathrm{ellPUnc}\right) = \mathrm{ppm}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{bigG},\,\mathrm{bigGUnc}\right) \land 2 \cdot \mathrm{ppm}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{tP},\,\mathrm{tPUnc}\right) = \mathrm{ppm}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{bigG},\,\mathrm{bigGUnc}\right) \land 2 \cdot \mathrm{ppm}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{mP},\,\mathrm{mPUnc}\right) = \mathrm{ppm}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{bigG},\,\mathrm{bigGUnc}\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 2 · AND IT IS EXACTLY HALF THE CONSTANT THEY ARE BUILT FROM ─────────────────────────────────────────── G is known to 22 parts per million; every Planck unit to 11. The factor is the square root, which halves a relative error, and it comes out exact on the published digits. This is the one relation in this file that is a relation and not a coincidence — and it is a fact about how uncertainty propagates, not about nature.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-the_measurement_admits_thirty_seven_values_and_not_one">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 277</strong> (<code>the_measurement_admits_thirty_seven_values_and_not_one</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_the_measurement_admits_thirty_seven_values_and_not_one">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>window</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>37</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>head</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>window</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>some</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>ellP</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>ellPUnc</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>last</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>window</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>some</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>ellP</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>ellPUnc</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>window.length = 37 ∧ window.head? = some (ellP - ellPUnc) ∧ window.getLast? = some (ellP + ellPUnc)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\mathrm{window}\right| = 37 \land \operatorname{head}\left(\mathrm{window}\right) = \mathrm{some}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{ellP} - \mathrm{ellPUnc}\right) \land \operatorname{last}\left(\mathrm{window}\right) = \mathrm{some}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{ellP} + \mathrm{ellPUnc}\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-the_digital_root_tracks_the_unit_and_not_the_scale">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 278</strong> (<code>the_digital_root_tracks_the_unit_and_not_the_scale</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_the_digital_root_tracks_the_unit_and_not_the_scale">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>dr</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>ellP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>dr</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>tP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>dr</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>mP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>dr</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>ellP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>dr</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>tP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>dr</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>tP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>dr</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>mP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>dr ellP = 8 ∧ dr tP = 4 ∧ dr mP = 9 ∧ dr ellP ≠ dr tP ∧ dr tP ≠ dr mP</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{dr}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{ellP}\right) = 8 \land \mathrm{dr}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{tP}\right) = 4 \land \mathrm{dr}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{mP}\right) = 9 \land \mathrm{dr}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{ellP}\right) \neq \mathrm{dr}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{tP}\right) \land \mathrm{dr}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{tP}\right) \neq \mathrm{dr}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{mP}\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-the_orbit_holds_two_thirds_of_the_ring_so_landing_on_it_says_little">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 279</strong> (<code>the_orbit_holds_two_thirds_of_the_ring_so_landing_on_it_says_little</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_the_orbit_holds_two_thirds_of_the_ring_so_landing_on_it_says_little">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>orbit</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>axis</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>orbit</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>axis</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>dr</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>ellP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>orbit</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>dr</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>tP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>orbit</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>dr</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>mP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>axis</mi></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>orbit.length = 6 ∧ axis.length = 3 ∧ orbit.length + axis.length = 9 ∧ orbit.contains (dr ellP) ∧ orbit.contains (dr tP) ∧ axis.contains (dr mP)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\mathrm{orbit}\right| = 6 \land \left|\mathrm{axis}\right| = 3 \land \left|\mathrm{orbit}\right| + \left|\mathrm{axis}\right| = 9 \land \mathrm{dr}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{ellP}\right) \in \mathrm{orbit} \land \mathrm{dr}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{tP}\right) \in \mathrm{orbit} \land \mathrm{dr}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{mP}\right) \in \mathrm{axis}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-no_product_of_three_lattice_constants_lands_where_the_planck_length_is">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 280</strong> (<code>no_product_of_three_lattice_constants_lands_where_the_planck_length_is</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_no_product_of_three_lattice_constants_lands_where_the_planck_length_is">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>products</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2197</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>products</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>ellP</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>ellPUnc</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∨</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mi>ellP</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>ellPUnc</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>products.length = 2197 ∧ products.all (fun v =&gt; v &lt; ellP - ellPUnc || v &gt; ellP + ellPUnc)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\mathrm{products}\right| = 2197 \land \forall v \in \mathrm{products},\; v &lt; \mathrm{ellP} - \mathrm{ellPUnc} \lor v &gt; \mathrm{ellP} + \mathrm{ellPUnc}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-the_same_search_does_reach_the_magnitude">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 281</strong> (<code>the_same_search_does_reach_the_magnitude</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_the_same_search_does_reach_the_magnitude">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>products</mi><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>1600000</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>1700000</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(products.filter (fun v =&gt; 1600000 ≤ v &amp;&amp; v ≤ 1700000)).length = 9</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\{\, v \in \mathrm{products} \mid 1600000 \le v \land v \le 1700000 \,\}\right| = 9</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 7 · AND THE SEARCH WAS LIVE, NOT VACUOUS ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── A search that produces nothing anywhere near the target proves nothing about the target. Nine of the same products land in the decade around the Planck length, so the silence in theorem 6 is a silence about the window and not about the magnitude. This is the control, decided rather than asserted.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-a_search_expecting_less_than_one_hit_settles_nothing_either_way">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 282</strong> (<code>a_search_expecting_less_than_one_hit_settles_nothing_either_way</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_a_search_expecting_less_than_one_hit_settles_nothing_either_way">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>ellPUnc</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mn>100001</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>ellPUnc</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>100001</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>9 * (2 * ellPUnc + 1) / 100001 = 0 ∧ 9 * (2 * ellPUnc + 1) &lt; 100001</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\frac{9 \cdot 2 \cdot \mathrm{ellPUnc} + 1}{100001} = 0 \land 9 \cdot 2 \cdot \mathrm{ellPUnc} + 1 &lt; 100001</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 8 · SO THE ZERO IS NOT EVIDENCE, AND NEITHER WOULD A ONE HAVE BEEN (SUPERSEDED BY 17) ─────────────── Kept as written and not withdrawn. It is true, and it is the weaker of the two reasons the search found nothing: theorem 17 gives the real one. A record that edits out the first answer hides how it was got. The honest reading of theorem 6, and the reason this file claims nothing from it. Spread those nine products uniformly over the 100,001 integers of that decade and the expected number landing in a window 37 wide is 9 * 37 / 100001, which is zero in the naturals — far under one. A search whose expected yield is below one finds nothing whether or not there is anything to find. The absence is reported; it is not promoted to a result, and a hit would not have been promoted either.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-every_planck_unit_is_a_square_root_and_not_a_plain_product">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 283</strong> (<code>every_planck_unit_is_a_square_root_and_not_a_plain_product</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_every_planck_unit_is_a_square_root_and_not_a_plain_product">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>dimEllP</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>mod</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>dimTP</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>mod</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>dimMP</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>mod</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>dimEllP.1 % 2 ≠ 0 ∧ dimTP.1 % 2 ≠ 0 ∧ dimMP.1 % 2 ≠ 0</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{dimEllP}_{1} \bmod 2 \neq 0 \land \mathrm{dimTP}_{1} \bmod 2 \neq 0 \land \mathrm{dimMP}_{1} \bmod 2 \neq 0</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-length_over_time_cancels_both_and_leaves_the_defined_constant">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 284</strong> (<code>length_over_time_cancels_both_and_leaves_the_defined_constant</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_length_over_time_cancels_both_and_leaves_the_defined_constant">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>ddiv</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>dimEllP</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>dimTP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>ddiv dimEllP dimTP = (0, 0, 2)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{ddiv}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{dimEllP},\,\mathrm{dimTP}\right) = \left(0,\,0,\,2\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 10 · LENGTH OVER TIME CANCELS BOTH ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Dividing the Planck length by the Planck time subtracts the exponents: the quantum vanishes, gravity vanishes, and what is left is c to the first power — a constant the SI fixes exactly. There is no measurement anywhere in this combination.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-length_times_mass_cancels_gravity_and_leaves_the_quantum">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 285</strong> (<code>length_times_mass_cancels_gravity_and_leaves_the_quantum</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_length_times_mass_cancels_gravity_and_leaves_the_quantum">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>dmul</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>dimEllP</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>dimMP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>dmul dimEllP dimMP = (2, 0, -2)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{dmul}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{dimEllP},\,\mathrm{dimMP}\right) = \left(2,\,0,\,-2\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 11 · LENGTH TIMES MASS CANCELS GRAVITY ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Multiplying adds the exponents, and G's cancel against each other: hbar to the first, c to the minus first. Pure quantum — and since the SI fixes h exactly, this combination is exact too.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-length_over_mass_cancels_the_quantum_and_leaves_gravity">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 286</strong> (<code>length_over_mass_cancels_the_quantum_and_leaves_gravity</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_length_over_mass_cancels_the_quantum_and_leaves_gravity">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>ddiv</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>dimEllP</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>dimMP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>ddiv dimEllP dimMP = (0, 2, -4)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{ddiv}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{dimEllP},\,\mathrm{dimMP}\right) = \left(0,\,2,\,-4\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 12 · LENGTH OVER MASS CANCELS THE QUANTUM ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── The other way round, hbar cancels and G survives at full strength — not halved, doubled back up, because the square root in the numerator meets the inverse square root in the denominator. Pure gravity, and the only one of the three that touches anything measured.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-the_gravitational_exponent_predicts_every_published_uncertainty">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 287</strong> (<code>the_gravitational_exponent_predicts_every_published_uncertainty</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_the_gravitational_exponent_predicts_every_published_uncertainty">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>gPpm</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>dimEllP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>gPpm</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>dimTP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>gPpm</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>dimMP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>gPpm</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>ddiv</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>dimEllP</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>dimTP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>gPpm</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>dmul</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>dimEllP</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>dimMP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>gPpm</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>ddiv</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>dimEllP</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>dimMP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ppm</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>bigG</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>bigGUnc</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>gPpm dimEllP = 11 ∧ gPpm dimTP = 11 ∧ gPpm dimMP = 11 ∧ gPpm (ddiv dimEllP dimTP) = 0 ∧ gPpm (dmul dimEllP dimMP) = 0 ∧ gPpm (ddiv dimEllP dimMP) = ppm bigG bigGUnc</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{gPpm}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{dimEllP}\right) = 11 \land \mathrm{gPpm}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{dimTP}\right) = 11 \land \mathrm{gPpm}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{dimMP}\right) = 11 \land \mathrm{gPpm}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{ddiv}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{dimEllP},\,\mathrm{dimTP}\right)\right) = 0 \land \mathrm{gPpm}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{dmul}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{dimEllP},\,\mathrm{dimMP}\right)\right) = 0 \land \mathrm{gPpm}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{ddiv}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{dimEllP},\,\mathrm{dimMP}\right)\right) = \mathrm{ppm}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{bigG},\,\mathrm{bigGUnc}\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-the_three_uncertainties_are_one_uncertainty_wearing_three_faces">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 288</strong> (<code>the_three_uncertainties_are_one_uncertainty_wearing_three_faces</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_the_three_uncertainties_are_one_uncertainty_wearing_three_faces">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><msub><mrow><mi>ddiv</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>dimEllP</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>dimTP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><msub><msub><mrow><mi>dmul</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>dimEllP</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>dimMP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><msub><msub><mrow><mi>ddiv</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>dimEllP</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>dimMP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(ddiv dimEllP dimTP).2.1 = 0 ∧ (dmul dimEllP dimMP).2.1 = 0 ∧ (ddiv dimEllP dimMP).2.1 ≠ 0</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{ddiv}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{dimEllP},\,\mathrm{dimTP}\right)_{2}_{1} = 0 \land \mathrm{dmul}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{dimEllP},\,\mathrm{dimMP}\right)_{2}_{1} = 0 \land \mathrm{ddiv}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{dimEllP},\,\mathrm{dimMP}\right)_{2}_{1} \neq 0</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 14 · SO TWO OF THE THREE CONTAIN NO MEASUREMENT AT ALL ──────────────────────────────────────────────── Which means the three published uncertainties are not three independent numbers. They are ONE number — G's — appearing in each unit under a square root. Theorem 1 read them as a shared 11; that reading was right about the arithmetic and thin about the cause, and this is the cause.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-the_published_digits_miss_an_identity_that_has_no_measurement_in_it">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 289</strong> (<code>the_published_digits_miss_an_identity_that_has_no_measurement_in_it</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_the_published_digits_miss_an_identity_that_has_no_measurement_in_it">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>ratioFromDigits</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>299792422</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mi>ratioFromDigits</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>cDefined</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>cDefined</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>ratioFromDigits</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>ratioFromDigits = 299792422 ∧ ratioFromDigits ≠ cDefined ∧ cDefined - ratioFromDigits = 36</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{ratioFromDigits} = 299792422 \land \mathrm{ratioFromDigits} \neq \mathrm{cDefined} \land \mathrm{cDefined} - \mathrm{ratioFromDigits} = 36</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-the_miss_is_rounding_and_sits_far_below_the_uncertainty">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 290</strong> (<code>the_miss_is_rounding_and_sits_far_below_the_uncertainty</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_the_miss_is_rounding_and_sits_far_below_the_uncertainty">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>cDefined</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>ratioFromDigits</mi></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mn>1000000</mn></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>cDefined</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>cDefined</mi></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>cDefined</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>ratioFromDigits</mi></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mn>1000000</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>91</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(cDefined - ratioFromDigits) * 1000000 &lt; 11 * cDefined ∧ 11 * cDefined / ((cDefined - ratioFromDigits) * 1000000) = 91</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{cDefined} - \mathrm{ratioFromDigits} \cdot 1000000 &lt; 11 \cdot \mathrm{cDefined} \land \frac{11 \cdot \mathrm{cDefined}}{\mathrm{cDefined} - \mathrm{ratioFromDigits} \cdot 1000000} = 91</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 16 · AND THE MISS IS ROUNDING, WHICH IS WHY IT IS INVISIBLE ─────────────────────────────────────────── 36 m/s in 299792458 is 0.12 parts per million. The measurement uncertainty on these units is 11 — ninety one times larger. Each value is rounded to seven significant figures before publication, and a ratio of two independently rounded numbers cannot reproduce an exact constant. Nothing is wrong with the physics or with CODATA: the deviation is a fact about DECIMAL PRESENTATION, it sits two orders below the uncertainty, and it is invisible in every use of these constants except this one — asking an exact identity to hold on the printed digits.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-not_one_value_the_world_admits_is_reachable_from_this_lattice">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 291</strong> (<code>not_one_value_the_world_admits_is_reachable_from_this_lattice</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_not_one_value_the_world_admits_is_reachable_from_this_lattice">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>window</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mi>reachable</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>window.all (fun v =&gt; ! reachable v)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall v \in \mathrm{window},\; \lnot \mathrm{reachable}\mathopen{}\left(v\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-every_seed_factors_over_those_primes_so_every_product_does">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 292</strong> (<code>every_seed_factors_over_those_primes_so_every_product_does</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_every_seed_factors_over_those_primes_so_every_product_does">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>seeds</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>reachable</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>seeds.all (fun s =&gt; reachable s)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall s \in \mathrm{seeds},\; \mathrm{reachable}\mathopen{}\left(s\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 18 · AND THE SEEDS CARRY EXACTLY THOSE PRIMES ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── The other half of theorem 17, without which it is an assertion about a list rather than about the lattice: every seed really does strip to 1 over those five primes, so the closure is complete and the unreachability follows for products of any depth, not only for the three-deep search actually run.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-the_exponent_predicts_the_registry_with_a_literal_on_neither_side">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 293</strong> (<code>the_exponent_predicts_the_registry_with_a_literal_on_neither_side</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_the_exponent_predicts_the_registry_with_a_literal_on_neither_side">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>gPpm</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>dimEllP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ppm</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>ellP</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ellPUnc</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>gPpm</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>dimTP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ppm</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>tP</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>tPUnc</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>gPpm</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>dimMP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ppm</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>mP</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>mPUnc</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>gPpm dimEllP = ppm ellP ellPUnc ∧ gPpm dimTP = ppm tP tPUnc ∧ gPpm dimMP = ppm mP mPUnc</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{gPpm}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{dimEllP}\right) = \mathrm{ppm}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{ellP},\,\mathrm{ellPUnc}\right) \land \mathrm{gPpm}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{dimTP}\right) = \mathrm{ppm}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{tP},\,\mathrm{tPUnc}\right) \land \mathrm{gPpm}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{dimMP}\right) = \mathrm{ppm}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{mP},\,\mathrm{mPUnc}\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 19 · THE UNCERTAINTY PREDICTION, WITH NOTHING TYPED ON EITHER SIDE ──────────────────────────────────── Theorem 13 is true and decides less than its name claims: `gPpm` has 11 written into it, so five of its six conjuncts compare a literal with itself. Here both sides are derived — the left from the dimensional exponents, the right from the CODATA digit sequences — so the prediction is tested against the registry.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-the_exact_halving_survives_only_because_the_division_truncated">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 294</strong> (<code>the_exact_halving_survives_only_because_the_division_truncated</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_the_exact_halving_survives_only_because_the_division_truncated">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>ppm4</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>ellP</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ellPUnc</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>111368</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ppm4</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>bigG</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>bigGUnc</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>224742</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>ppm4</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>ellP</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ellPUnc</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>ppm4</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>bigG</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>bigGUnc</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>ppm4 ellP ellPUnc = 111368 ∧ ppm4 bigG bigGUnc = 224742 ∧ 2 * ppm4 ellP ellPUnc ≠ ppm4 bigG bigGUnc</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{ppm4}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{ellP},\,\mathrm{ellPUnc}\right) = 111368 \land \mathrm{ppm4}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{bigG},\,\mathrm{bigGUnc}\right) = 224742 \land 2 \cdot \mathrm{ppm4}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{ellP},\,\mathrm{ellPUnc}\right) \neq \mathrm{ppm4}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{bigG},\,\mathrm{bigGUnc}\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-no_power_of_ten_moves_the_root">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 295</strong> (<code>no_power_of_ten_moves_the_root</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_no_power_of_ten_moves_the_root">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>dr</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>ellP</mi><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>dr</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>ellP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 8).all (fun k =&gt; dr (ellP * 10 ^ k) = dr ellP)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall k \in \{0,\dots,7\},\; \mathrm{dr}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{ellP} \cdot 10^{k}\right) = \mathrm{dr}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{ellP}\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 21 · A DIGITAL ROOT CANNOT BE MOVED BY A METRIC PREFIX ──────────────────────────────────────────────── Theorem 4's prose offered the other SI units as the falsifier for reading dr(1616255) = 8 as meaningful. They are not one scale in three units — a length, a time and a mass are three quantities — and worse, a root is invariant under multiplication by ten, so metre, centimetre, femtometre and angstrom all give 8. The prefix argument could never have falsified anything, and is refused here rather than left standing.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 8 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-an_exactly_defined_non_decimal_unit_moves_the_root">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 296</strong> (<code>an_exactly_defined_non_decimal_unit_moves_the_root</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_an_exactly_defined_non_decimal_unit_moves_the_root">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>ellPInches</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>63632086614</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>dr</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>ellPInches</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>dr</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>ellPInches</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>dr</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>ellP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>ellPInches = 63632086614 ∧ dr ellPInches = 9 ∧ dr ellPInches ≠ dr ellP</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{ellPInches} = 63632086614 \land \mathrm{dr}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{ellPInches}\right) = 9 \land \mathrm{dr}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{ellPInches}\right) \neq \mathrm{dr}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{ellP}\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-the_miss_fits_inside_the_printed_precision_and_not_inside_the_measurement">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 297</strong> (<code>the_miss_fits_inside_the_printed_precision_and_not_inside_the_measurement</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_the_miss_fits_inside_the_printed_precision_and_not_inside_the_measurement">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>displayBudget</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>120</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>cDefined</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>ratioFromDigits</mi></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>displayBudget</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>displayBudget</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mn>10000</mn></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>cDefined</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>displayBudget = 120 ∧ cDefined - ratioFromDigits ≤ displayBudget ∧ displayBudget * 10000 &lt; 11 * cDefined</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{displayBudget} = 120 \land \mathrm{cDefined} - \mathrm{ratioFromDigits} \le \mathrm{displayBudget} \land \mathrm{displayBudget} \cdot 10000 &lt; 11 \cdot \mathrm{cDefined}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-planck-the_planck_mantissa_factors_outside_the_lattice">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 298</strong> (<code>the_planck_mantissa_factors_outside_the_lattice</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_planck_the_planck_mantissa_factors_outside_the_lattice">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>ellP</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>323251</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>569</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>323251</mn><mo>mod</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mi>reachable</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>ellP</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>ellP = 5 * 323251 ∧ (List.range' 2 568).all (fun d =&gt; 323251 % d ≠ 0) ∧ ! reachable ellP</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{ellP} = 5 \cdot 323251 \land \forall d \in \{2,\dots,569\},\; 323251 \bmod d \neq 0 \land \lnot \mathrm{reachable}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{ellP}\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 24 · THE MANTISSA ITSELF IS OUT OF REACH ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── The narrowest statement of theorem 17, at the single value a coincidence would have to hit: the Planck length's published mantissa is 5 x 323251, and 323251 is prime — it is not 2, 3, 5, 7 or 17, and nothing built from those can produce it. Decided by exhibiting the factorisation and refusing every divisor up to the square root, so the primality is checked here and not asserted.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 568 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>


### Order-invariance {#quantum}

<p class="paper-src"><code>src/proof/quantum.lean</code> · namespace <code>Quantum</code> · 12 theorems</p>

form is invariant under permutation of its input, which is why `receipt_is_order_invariant` holds. What
  this file contributes is the Lean verification over a stated finite domain and the negative controls
  beside it — `naive_fold_is_not_order_invariant` shows the property is bought by the sort and not free,
  and `the_receipt_is_not_injective` and `the_invariance_is_canonicalisation_not_physics` state its limits.
  Verification and refusal, not discovery.
prior_art_search: literature search performed 2026-09-05, terms "sorted Merkle tree order-invariant set
  commitment canonical ordering leaves"; prior art found and credited. This file was `unclassified` — no
  search had ever been run for it — and it is one of the 8 files whose 86 theorems are staged for DOIs.
prior_art_pool: mixed
  canonicalisation before folding is a searchable technique; the receipt it folds is ours.
  BOUNDED means a search is well posed and simply has not been run — the row is unclassified because
  nobody looked. UNBOUNDED means the subject is this artifact, so there is no pool to search and the
  row will stay unclassified however much work is done. They look identical in a count and need
  opposite responses, which is the distinction uuidna-49 asked for and nobody had drawn.
prior_art_own: order-invariance of this deposit's receipt
The quantum receipt — order invariance, proved rather than asserted.


"Quantum" here is a STRUCTURAL claim and nothing more: a set of perspectives held at once (superposition),
each collapsing to one observation, and a receipt that is the SAME for every observer regardless of the
order they observe in. No hardware, no speedup, no physics. The deposit asserted this order-invariance in
prose and in TypeScript; it is proved here, by decide, over every permutation — no anchors, no axioms,
no Mathlib.

It also proves the CONTRAST: an order-dependent fold is genuinely not invariant. Without that, the
invariance theorem could hold vacuously for a fold that ignores its input, which is the failure mode this
file exists to avoid. Integrity, not truth.

settledHere := 11
ghzXSupport := [0, 3, 5, 6]</code></pre>

<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>ghzXSupport</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>

<p class="thm-remark">And it is HALF of them — so the measurement carries one bit that the computational basis does not.</p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-quantum-a_classical_mixture_reaches_the_parity_ghz_never_does">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 310</strong> (<code>a_classical_mixture_reaches_the_parity_ghz_never_does</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_quantum_a_classical_mixture_reaches_the_parity_ghz_never_does">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>par3</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>par3</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ghzXSupport</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>((List.range 8).filter (fun n =&gt; par3 n == 1)).length = 4 ∧ ((List.range 8).filter (fun n =&gt; par3 n == 1)).all (fun n =&gt; ¬ ghzXSupport.contains n)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\{\, n \in \{0,\dots,7\} \mid \mathrm{par3}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) = 1 \,\}\right| = 4 \land \forall n \in \{\, n \in \{0,\dots,7\} \mid \mathrm{par3}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) = 1 \,\},\; \lnot n \in \mathrm{ghzXSupport}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">The discriminating fact: a classical mixture spreads over BOTH parities, so a parity that is always even is a fact about the state and not about the reporting. Odd-parity strings exist and GHZ never reaches them.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 64 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>


### What exhaustion reaches, and what lies outside it {#reach}

<p class="paper-src"><code>src/proof/reach.lean</code> · namespace <code>Reach</code> · 12 theorems</p>

old as mathematics; the deposit claims none of it. What is its own here is the decision over its OWN
  bounds, and the statement of where that decision stops.


THE QUESTION, asked directly: does a `by decide` proof of a Clay conjecture exist in this deposit?

The honest way to answer is not prose. `by decide` proves a proposition by walking its domain and
reporting what it found; it needs a Decidable instance, and it gets one by the domain being finite. Every
theorem in this tree is of that kind, and the largest domain any of them walks is 152,568,360,000 cases.
Each of the seven Clay conjectures quantifies over an infinite set. So the question is whether an
exhaustion can reach past its own bound.

It cannot, and that is decided below at fifty bounds: for each n, walking the first n naturals does not
reach n. Not once, at a flattering bound — at every one of them.

WHAT IS NOT PROVED HERE, said as plainly as what is. This decides the statement AT FIFTY BOUNDS. The
universal "for every n" needs induction, and induction is not exhaustion — it is the tactic this deposit
does not use, because its rule is that a theorem walks its domain. So the file demonstrates the boundary
at every bound it checks and does not claim the quantifier. A reader who wants the universal has it from
Euclid and does not need this deposit for it.

The answer to the question, then: no. Not because the seven are hard, and not because the effort was not
made — because the method reaches exactly as far as it counts, and a conjecture over an infinite domain
lies outside every count. That is a fact about `decide`, not a verdict on the conjectures.

<p class="paper-h">Definitions</p>

<pre class="thm-statement paper-defs"><code>bounds := List.range' 1 50
largestDomainHere := 152568360000</code></pre>

<div class="thm" id="thm-reach-exhaustion_never_reaches_its_own_bound">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 311</strong> (<code>exhaustion_never_reaches_its_own_bound</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_reach_exhaustion_never_reaches_its_own_bound">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>bounds</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>bounds.all (fun n =&gt; (List.range n).length == n &amp;&amp; ¬ (List.range n).contains n)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \mathrm{bounds},\; \left|\{0,\dots,n-1\}\right| = n \land \lnot n \in \{0,\dots,n-1\}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 1 · AN EXHAUSTION DOES NOT REACH ITS OWN BOUND ────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Walking the first n naturals produces exactly n of them, and n is not among them. Checked at fifty bounds, so this is not one convenient n.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-reach-the_successor_of_every_bound_lies_outside">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 312</strong> (<code>the_successor_of_every_bound_lies_outside</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_reach_the_successor_of_every_bound_lies_outside">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>bounds</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>bounds.all (fun n =&gt; ¬ (List.range n).contains (n + 1))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \mathrm{bounds},\; \lnot n + 1 \in \{0,\dots,n-1\}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 2 · AND SOMETHING ALWAYS LIES OUTSIDE ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── The successor of the bound is outside the walk, at every bound checked. This is the shape of the whole limit: whatever finite domain a theorem here exhausts, the naturals continue past it.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-reach-doubling_the_domain_leaves_the_same_hole">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 313</strong> (<code>doubling_the_domain_leaves_the_same_hole</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_reach_doubling_the_domain_leaves_the_same_hole">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>bounds</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>bounds.all (fun n =&gt; ¬ (List.range (2 * n)).contains (2 * n))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \mathrm{bounds},\; \lnot 2 \cdot n \in \{0,\dots,2 \cdot n-1\}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 3 · GROWING THE BOUND DOES NOT CLOSE THE GAP ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Doubling the domain leaves the same hole. An exhaustion is not made complete by being made larger, which is why no amount of compute turns this method into a proof over an infinite domain.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-reach-the_successor_leaves_every_domain_and_the_predecessor_returns">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 314</strong> (<code>the_successor_leaves_every_domain_and_the_predecessor_returns</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_reach_the_successor_leaves_every_domain_and_the_predecessor_returns">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>bounds</mi><mo>⧺</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>largestDomainHere</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(bounds ++ [largestDomainHere]).all (fun n =&gt; n + 1 &gt; n &amp;&amp; (n + 1) - 1 == n &amp;&amp; (n + 1) % 2 != n % 2)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \mathrm{bounds} \mathbin{+\!\!+} [\mathrm{largestDomainHere}],\; n + 1 &gt; n \land n + 1 - 1 = n \land n + 1 \bmod 2 \neq n \bmod 2</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-reach-the_predecessor_returns_every_successor">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 315</strong> (<code>the_predecessor_returns_every_successor</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_reach_the_predecessor_returns_every_successor">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ n : Nat, (n + 1) - 1 = n</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── AND FOR EVERY n, WHICH NO EXHAUSTION ABOVE CAN SAY. The file's point is that `decide` stops at its bound; this is what goes past it: a PROOF that the predecessor returns every successor, for all naturals at once. It is the only kind of statement that reaches an unbounded domain, and it rests on the standard axiom propext, printed by lean.ts. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-reach-exhaustion_never_reaches_its_own_bound_for_every_n">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 316</strong> (<code>exhaustion_never_reaches_its_own_bound_for_every_n</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_reach_exhaustion_never_reaches_its_own_bound_for_every_n">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ n : Nat, (List.range n).length = n ∧ n ∉ List.range n</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the three bounded rows above, proved for every bound — no list of bounds ───────────────────────────────── the file's own point, now without a range: no exhaustion over 0..n-1 contains n, n + 1, or (at 2n) 2n.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

### The constants, derived from what they are {#roots}

<p class="paper-src"><code>src/proof/roots.lean</code> · namespace <code>Roots</code> · 8 theorems</p>

fractional part of the cube root of the t-th prime (§4.2.3) and H[i] the same of the square root
  (§5.3.5). Newton's method for integer roots is classical. Neither is this deposit's. What is decided
  here is only that THIS deposit's derivation computes those definitions and not something near them.


src/0/sha512.ts used to carry eighty-eight hexadecimal literals. It computes them now, from the
definition FIPS gives — and that trade is only a gain if the computation is right. A wrong root gives a
hash that is self-consistent, round-trips perfectly, and is not SHA-512; the old literals at least had
the property that someone had once copied them from the standard.

So the derivation is decided here, and the pins below are the point rather than a lapse: `merge_agrees`
in merkle.lean does the same thing for the fold. A published value written down and compared against a
computation is an AGREEMENT check, which is the opposite of a typed constant standing in for one.

No axioms, no Mathlib, no sorry.

<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>firstPrimes</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>17</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>19</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>firstPrimes</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>isPrime</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>19</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>isPrime</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>firstPrimes 40 8 = [2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19] ∧ (firstPrimes 40 8).all isPrime ∧ ((List.range' 2 18).filter isPrime).length = 8</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{firstPrimes}\mathopen{}\left(40,\,8\right) = [2,\,3,\,5,\,7,\,11,\,13,\,17,\,19] \land \forall x \in \mathrm{firstPrimes}\mathopen{}\left(40,\,8\right),\; \mathrm{isPrime}\mathopen{}\left(x\right) \land \left|\{\, x \in \{2,\dots,19\} \mid \mathrm{isPrime}\mathopen{}\left(x\right) \,\}\right| = 8</code></pre></details>
