settledHere := 32</code></pre>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-euclids_form_is_perfect_at_every_mersenne_prime_to_seven">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 363</strong> (<code>euclids_form_is_perfect_at_every_mersenne_prime_to_seven</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_euclids_form_is_perfect_at_every_mersenne_prime_to_seven">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mi>isPrime</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>p</mi></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∨</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>properDivisorSum</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>p</mi></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>p</mi></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>[2, 3, 5, 7].all (fun p =&gt; !(isPrime (2 ^ p - 1)) || properDivisorSum (2 ^ (p - 1) * (2 ^ p - 1)) == 2 ^ (p - 1) * (2 ^ p - 1))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall p \in [2,\,3,\,5,\,7],\; \lnot \mathrm{isPrime}\mathopen{}\left(2^{p} - 1\right) \lor \mathrm{properDivisorSum}\mathopen{}\left(2^{p - 1} \cdot 2^{p} - 1\right) = 2^{p - 1} \cdot 2^{p} - 1</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 4 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_mersenne_hypothesis_is_real_at_eleven">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 364</strong> (<code>the_mersenne_hypothesis_is_real_at_eleven</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_mersenne_hypothesis_is_real_at_eleven">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>isPrime</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>11</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>false</mi></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>23</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>89</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>11</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>isPrime (2 ^ 11 - 1) = false ∧ 23 * 89 = 2 ^ 11 - 1</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{isPrime}\mathopen{}\left(2^{11} - 1\right) = \mathrm{false} \land 23 \cdot 89 = 2^{11} - 1</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── and the hypothesis is not decoration: at p = 11 the Mersenne number is composite ───────────────────── Without this, the theorem above is four cases where the guard happens to be true, and a reader has no way to see that the guard ever does anything. 2^11 − 1 = 2047 = 23 · 89.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_amicable_pair_is_mutual_and_neither_is_perfect">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 365</strong> (<code>the_amicable_pair_is_mutual_and_neither_is_perfect</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_amicable_pair_is_mutual_and_neither_is_perfect">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>properDivisorSum</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>220</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>284</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>properDivisorSum</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>284</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>220</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>properDivisorSum</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>220</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>220</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>properDivisorSum</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>284</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>284</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>properDivisorSum 220 = 284 ∧ properDivisorSum 284 = 220 ∧ properDivisorSum 220 ≠ 220 ∧ properDivisorSum 284 ≠ 284</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{properDivisorSum}\mathopen{}\left(220\right) = 284 \land \mathrm{properDivisorSum}\mathopen{}\left(284\right) = 220 \land \mathrm{properDivisorSum}\mathopen{}\left(220\right) \neq 220 \land \mathrm{properDivisorSum}\mathopen{}\left(284\right) \neq 284</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_primitive_roots_mod_nine_are_exactly_two_and_five">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 366</strong> (<code>the_primitive_roots_mod_nine_are_exactly_two_and_five</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_primitive_roots_mod_nine_are_exactly_two_and_five">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ordMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(unitsMod 9).filter (fun g =&gt; ordMod g 9 == 6) = [2, 5]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\{\, g \in \mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right) \mid \mathrm{ordMod}\mathopen{}\left(g,\,9\right) = 6 \,\} = [2,\,5]</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the primitive roots mod nine are exactly two and five ──────────────────────────────────────────────── families.lean decides that a primitive root EXISTS at 9. Which ones they are is a different statement, and the ledger's row claims the stronger one: a residue is a primitive root exactly when its powers run through all six units, and only 2 and 5 do.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 2 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_eisenstein_units_are_exactly_six">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 367</strong> (<code>the_eisenstein_units_are_exactly_six</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_eisenstein_units_are_exactly_six">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(((List.range 7).flatMap (fun (i : Nat) =&gt; (List.range 7).map (fun (j : Nat) =&gt; (((i : Int) - 3, (j : Int) - 3) : Int × Int)))).filter (fun p =&gt; eisensteinNorm p.1 p.2 == 1)).length = 6</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the Eisenstein integers have exactly six units ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── The units are the norm-1 elements. Searched over the box −3…3 in both coordinates, which is wider than it needs to be: the norm is a positive definite form, so nothing outside can have norm 1, and finding exactly six inside a box that could have held more is the content.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 49 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_subtraction_game_loses_exactly_at_the_multiples_of_four">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 368</strong> (<code>the_subtraction_game_loses_exactly_at_the_multiples_of_four</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_subtraction_game_loses_exactly_at_the_multiples_of_four">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∨</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>if</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>;</mo><mo>otherwise</mo><mrow><mo>∃</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 41).all (fun n =&gt; if n % 4 == 0 then [1, 2, 3].all (fun m =&gt; !(m ≤ n) || (n - m) % 4 != 0) else [1, 2, 3].any (fun m =&gt; m ≤ n &amp;&amp; (n - m) % 4 == 0))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{0,\dots,40\},\; \begin{cases}\forall m \in [1,\,2,\,3],\; \lnot m \le n \lor n - m \bmod 4 \neq 0 &amp; \text{if } n \bmod 4 = 0\\ \exists m \in [1,\,2,\,3] : m \le n \land n - m \bmod 4 = 0 &amp; \text{otherwise}\end{cases}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the subtraction game {1,2,3}: the mover loses exactly at the multiples of four ─────────────────────── Both halves, which is what makes it the theorem rather than a pattern: from a multiple of four every legal move leaves a non-multiple, and from a non-multiple some legal move reaches one.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 369 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_units_of_z9_form_three_pairs_summing_to_nine">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 369</strong> (<code>the_units_of_z9_form_three_pairs_summing_to_nine</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_units_of_z9_form_three_pairs_summing_to_nine">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>-</mo><mi>u</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>-</mo><mi>u</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>-</mo><mi>u</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>((unitsMod 9).filter (fun u =&gt; u &lt; 9 - u)).length = 3 ∧ (unitsMod 9).all (fun u =&gt; (unitsMod 9).contains (9 - u) &amp;&amp; u + (9 - u) == 9)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\{\, u \in \mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right) \mid u &lt; 9 - u \,\}\right| = 3 \land \forall u \in \mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right),\; 9 - u \in \mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right) \land u + 9 - u = 9</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the six units fall into three additive-inverse pairs, each summing to nine ───────────────────────────</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_multiplication_table_of_the_z9_units_is_a_latin_square">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 370</strong> (<code>the_multiplication_table_of_the_z9_units_is_a_latin_square</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_multiplication_table_of_the_z9_units_is_a_latin_square">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>dedup</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>dedup</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(unitsMod 9).all (fun a =&gt; ((unitsMod 9).map (fun b =&gt; a * b % 9)).eraseDups.length == (unitsMod 9).length &amp;&amp; ((unitsMod 9).map (fun b =&gt; a * b % 9)).all (fun x =&gt; (unitsMod 9).contains x)) ∧ (unitsMod 9).all (fun b =&gt; ((unitsMod 9).map (fun a =&gt; a * b % 9)).eraseDups.length == (unitsMod 9).length &amp;&amp; ((unitsMod 9).map (fun a =&gt; a * b % 9)).all (fun x =&gt; (unitsMod 9).contains x))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall a \in \mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right),\; \left|\operatorname{dedup}\left(\{\, a \cdot b \bmod 9 \mid b \in \mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right) \,\}\right)\right| = \left|\mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right)\right| \land \forall x \in \{\, a \cdot b \bmod 9 \mid b \in \mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right) \,\},\; x \in \mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right) \land \forall b \in \mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right),\; \left|\operatorname{dedup}\left(\{\, a \cdot b \bmod 9 \mid a \in \mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right) \,\}\right)\right| = \left|\mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right)\right| \land \forall x \in \{\, a \cdot b \bmod 9 \mid a \in \mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right) \,\},\; x \in \mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the Cayley table is a Latin square: every row AND every column is a permutation of the units ───────── Rows alone would suffice in an abelian group, but only if commutativity were already stated. Both are decided here rather than one being inferred from something this theorem does not say.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_count_of_primitive_roots_is_phi_of_phi">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 371</strong> (<code>the_count_of_primitive_roots_is_phi_of_phi</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_count_of_primitive_roots_is_phi_of_phi">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mi>hasPrimitiveRoot</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∨</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ordMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>totient</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>totient</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 2 59).all (fun n =&gt; !(hasPrimitiveRoot n) || ((unitsMod n).filter (fun g =&gt; ordMod g n == (unitsMod n).length)).length == totient (totient n))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{2,\dots,60\},\; \lnot \mathrm{hasPrimitiveRoot}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) \lor \left|\{\, g \in \mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) \mid \mathrm{ordMod}\mathopen{}\left(g,\,n\right) = \left|\mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(n\right)\right| \,\}\right| = \mathrm{totient}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{totient}\mathopen{}\left(n\right)\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 59 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_order_spectrum_of_the_z9_units_realises_gauss_divisor_sum">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 372</strong> (<code>the_order_spectrum_of_the_z9_units_realises_gauss_divisor_sum</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_order_spectrum_of_the_z9_units_realises_gauss_divisor_sum">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>mod</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ordMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>totient</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>totient</mi><mo>[</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>mod</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>((List.range' 1 6).filter (fun d =&gt; 6 % d == 0)).all (fun d =&gt; ((unitsMod 9).filter (fun g =&gt; ordMod g 9 == d)).length == totient d) ∧ (((List.range' 1 6).filter (fun d =&gt; 6 % d == 0)).map totient).foldl (· + ·) 0 = 6</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall d \in \{\, d \in \{1,\dots,6\} \mid 6 \bmod d = 0 \,\},\; \left|\{\, g \in \mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right) \mid \mathrm{ordMod}\mathopen{}\left(g,\,9\right) = d \,\}\right| = \mathrm{totient}\mathopen{}\left(d\right) \land \sum \mathrm{totient}[\{\, d \in \{1,\dots,6\} \mid 6 \bmod d = 0 \,\}] = 6</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the order spectrum realises Gauss's divisor sum: φ(d) units of order d, and the φ's sum to the group ─ The divisors are computed, not listed: a typed [1, 2, 3, 6] would be the answer written into the question, and the second conjunct is Σ_{d | 6} φ(d) = 6, which is the statement the first one realises.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 36 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_product_of_the_units_is_minus_one_exactly_where_gauss_says">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 373</strong> (<code>the_product_of_the_units_is_minus_one_exactly_where_gauss_says</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_product_of_the_units_is_minus_one_exactly_where_gauss_says">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>fold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>↦</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>u</mi></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>if</mo><mrow><mi>gaussCyclic</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>;</mo><mo>otherwise</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 2 59).all (fun n =&gt; ((unitsMod n).foldl (fun a u =&gt; a * u % n) 1) == (if gaussCyclic n then n - 1 else 1))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{2,\dots,60\},\; \operatorname{fold}_{a,\,u \mapsto a \cdot u \bmod n}\left(\mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(n\right),\, 1\right) = \begin{cases}n - 1 &amp; \text{if } \mathrm{gaussCyclic}\mathopen{}\left(n\right)\\ 1 &amp; \text{otherwise}\end{cases}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 59 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-three_is_a_primitive_root_mod_seven_and_seven_is_six_plus_one">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 374</strong> (<code>three_is_a_primitive_root_mod_seven_and_seven_is_six_plus_one</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_three_is_a_primitive_root_mod_seven_and_seven_is_six_plus_one">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>ordMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>ordMod 3 7 = 6 ∧ (unitsMod 7).length = 6 ∧ (List.range 7).length = (unitsMod 7).length + 1</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{ordMod}\mathopen{}\left(3,\,7\right) = 6 \land \left|\mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(7\right)\right| = 6 \land \left|\{0,\dots,6\}\right| = \left|\mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(7\right)\right| + 1</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── three is a primitive root mod seven, and seven is six units plus the one non-unit ────────────────────</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 7 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_z9_unit_group_splits_as_reflection_times_trinity">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 375</strong> (<code>the_z9_unit_group_splits_as_reflection_times_trinity</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_z9_unit_group_splits_as_reflection_times_trinity">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>powMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>powMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>u</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>dedup</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mi>powMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>dedup</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mi>powMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(unitsMod 9).all (fun u =&gt; powMod u 3 9 * powMod u 4 9 % 9 == u) ∧ ((unitsMod 9).map (fun u =&gt; powMod u 3 9)).eraseDups.length = 2 ∧ ((unitsMod 9).map (fun u =&gt; powMod u 4 9)).eraseDups.length = 3</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall u \in \mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right),\; \mathrm{powMod}\mathopen{}\left(u,\,3,\,9\right) \cdot \mathrm{powMod}\mathopen{}\left(u,\,4,\,9\right) \bmod 9 = u \land \left|\operatorname{dedup}\left(\{\, \mathrm{powMod}\mathopen{}\left(u,\,3,\,9\right) \mid u \in \mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right) \,\}\right)\right| = 2 \land \left|\operatorname{dedup}\left(\{\, \mathrm{powMod}\mathopen{}\left(u,\,4,\,9\right) \mid u \in \mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right) \,\}\right)\right| = 3</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the order-six unit group splits as a reflection times a trinity ────────────────────────────────────── u ↦ (u³, u⁴) is the splitting, and it works because 3 + 4 = 7 ≡ 1 in the exponent group of order six. The two factors have two and three values, which is the C2 × C3 the Chinese remainder theorem predicts.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-an_odd_prime_is_a_sum_of_two_squares_exactly_when_it_is_one_mod_four">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 376</strong> (<code>an_odd_prime_is_a_sum_of_two_squares_exactly_when_it_is_one_mod_four</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_an_odd_prime_is_a_sum_of_two_squares_exactly_when_it_is_one_mod_four">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>isSumOfTwoSquares</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>199</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>isPrime</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>isSumOfTwoSquares</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>isSumOfTwoSquares 2 ∧ ((List.range' 3 197).filter isPrime).all (fun p =&gt; isSumOfTwoSquares p == (p % 4 == 1))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{isSumOfTwoSquares}\mathopen{}\left(2\right) \land \forall p \in \{\, x \in \{3,\dots,199\} \mid \mathrm{isPrime}\mathopen{}\left(x\right) \,\},\; \mathrm{isSumOfTwoSquares}\mathopen{}\left(p\right) = p \bmod 4 = 1</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 197 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_area_of_an_integer_right_triangle_is_a_multiple_of_six">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 377</strong> (<code>the_area_of_an_integer_right_triangle_is_a_multiple_of_six</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_area_of_an_integer_right_triangle_is_a_multiple_of_six">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mo>∃</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>:</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∨</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>mod</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 40).all (fun a =&gt; (List.range' 1 40).all (fun b =&gt; !((List.range' 1 60).any (fun c =&gt; a * a + b * b == c * c)) || (a * b / 2) % 6 == 0))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall a \in \{1,\dots,40\},\; \forall b \in \{1,\dots,40\},\; \lnot \exists c \in \{1,\dots,60\} : a \cdot a + b \cdot b = c \cdot c \lor \frac{a \cdot b}{2} \bmod 6 = 0</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 96,000 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_inverse_map_permutes_the_units_and_is_an_involution">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 378</strong> (<code>the_inverse_map_permutes_the_units_and_is_an_involution</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_inverse_map_permutes_the_units_and_is_an_involution">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>dedup</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>invUnit</mi><mo>[</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>invUnit</mi><mo>[</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>invUnit</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>invUnit</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>u</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>((unitsMod 9).map invUnit).eraseDups.length = (unitsMod 9).length ∧ ((unitsMod 9).map invUnit).all (fun x =&gt; (unitsMod 9).contains x) ∧ (unitsMod 9).all (fun u =&gt; invUnit (invUnit u) == u)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\operatorname{dedup}\left(\mathrm{invUnit}[\mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right)]\right)\right| = \left|\mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right)\right| \land \forall x \in \mathrm{invUnit}[\mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right)],\; x \in \mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right) \land \forall u \in \mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right),\; \mathrm{invUnit}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{invUnit}\mathopen{}\left(u\right)\right) = u</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the inverse map permutes the units and is its own inverse ───────────────────────────────────────────</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_hockey_stick_identity_holds_across_the_range">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 379</strong> (<code>the_hockey_stick_identity_holds_across_the_range</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_hockey_stick_identity_holds_across_the_range">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mi>choose</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>choose</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 11).all (fun r =&gt; (List.range 19).all (fun m =&gt; ((List.range' r (m + 1)).map (fun i =&gt; choose i r)).foldl (· + ·) 0 == choose (r + m + 1) (r + 1)))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall r \in \{0,\dots,10\},\; \forall m \in \{0,\dots,18\},\; \sum \{\, \mathrm{choose}\mathopen{}\left(i,\,r\right) \mid i \in \{r,\dots,r+m + 1-1\} \,\} = \mathrm{choose}\mathopen{}\left(r + m + 1,\,r + 1\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 209 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-three_is_the_only_prime_one_less_than_a_square_in_this_range">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 380</strong> (<code>three_is_the_only_prime_one_less_than_a_square_in_this_range</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_three_is_the_only_prime_one_less_than_a_square_in_this_range">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>41</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mi>isPrime</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>41</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>((List.range' 2 40).filter (fun n =&gt; isPrime (n * n - 1))) = [2] ∧ (List.range' 3 39).all (fun n =&gt; (n - 1) * (n + 1) == n * n - 1 &amp;&amp; n - 1 &gt; 1)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\{\, n \in \{2,\dots,41\} \mid \mathrm{isPrime}\mathopen{}\left(n \cdot n - 1\right) \,\} = [2] \land \forall n \in \{3,\dots,41\},\; n - 1 \cdot n + 1 = n \cdot n - 1 \land n - 1 &gt; 1</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── three is the only prime one less than a square, and the reason is the factorisation ───────────────── n² − 1 = (n−1)(n+1), and above n = 2 both factors exceed one. Decided over a range; the row claims it for every n, so the range does not carry it — the factorisation is the general argument and this is the check that the argument has no small counterexample.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 1,560 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-eight_times_a_triangular_number_plus_one_is_an_odd_square">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 381</strong> (<code>eight_times_a_triangular_number_plus_one_is_an_odd_square</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_eight_times_a_triangular_number_plus_one_is_an_odd_square">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>59</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 60).all (fun n =&gt; 8 * (n * (n + 1) / 2) + 1 == (2 * n + 1) * (2 * n + 1))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{0,\dots,59\},\; 8 \cdot \frac{n \cdot n + 1}{2} + 1 = 2 \cdot n + 1 \cdot 2 \cdot n + 1</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── eight triangular numbers and one make an odd square ─────────────────────────────────────────────────</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 60 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_powers_of_two_mod_nine_and_of_three_mod_seven_are_isomorphic">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 382</strong> (<code>the_powers_of_two_mod_nine_and_of_three_mod_seven_are_isomorphic</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_powers_of_two_mod_nine_and_of_three_mod_seven_are_isomorphic">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>dedup</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mi>powMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>dedup</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mi>powMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mi>powMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mi>powMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>powMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>powMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>powMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>powMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>powMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>powMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>((List.range 6).map (fun k =&gt; powMod 2 k 9)).eraseDups.length = 6 ∧ ((List.range 6).map (fun k =&gt; powMod 3 k 7)).eraseDups.length = 6 ∧ ((List.range 6).map (fun k =&gt; powMod 2 k 9)).all (fun x =&gt; (unitsMod 9).contains x) ∧ ((List.range 6).map (fun k =&gt; powMod 3 k 7)).all (fun x =&gt; (unitsMod 7).contains x) ∧ (List.range 6).all (fun i =&gt; (List.range 6).all (fun j =&gt; powMod 2 i 9 * powMod 2 j 9 % 9 == powMod 2 ((i + j) % 6) 9 &amp;&amp; powMod 3 i 7 * powMod 3 j 7 % 7 == powMod 3 ((i + j) % 6) 7))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\operatorname{dedup}\left(\{\, \mathrm{powMod}\mathopen{}\left(2,\,k,\,9\right) \mid k \in \{0,\dots,5\} \,\}\right)\right| = 6 \land \left|\operatorname{dedup}\left(\{\, \mathrm{powMod}\mathopen{}\left(3,\,k,\,7\right) \mid k \in \{0,\dots,5\} \,\}\right)\right| = 6 \land \forall x \in \{\, \mathrm{powMod}\mathopen{}\left(2,\,k,\,9\right) \mid k \in \{0,\dots,5\} \,\},\; x \in \mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right) \land \forall x \in \{\, \mathrm{powMod}\mathopen{}\left(3,\,k,\,7\right) \mid k \in \{0,\dots,5\} \,\},\; x \in \mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(7\right) \land \forall i \in \{0,\dots,5\},\; \forall j \in \{0,\dots,5\},\; \mathrm{powMod}\mathopen{}\left(2,\,i,\,9\right) \cdot \mathrm{powMod}\mathopen{}\left(2,\,j,\,9\right) \bmod 9 = \mathrm{powMod}\mathopen{}\left(2,\,i + j \bmod 6,\,9\right) \land \mathrm{powMod}\mathopen{}\left(3,\,i,\,7\right) \cdot \mathrm{powMod}\mathopen{}\left(3,\,j,\,7\right) \bmod 7 = \mathrm{powMod}\mathopen{}\left(3,\,i + j \bmod 6,\,7\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the vortex and the rosette carry the same group: 2^k mod 9 ↦ 3^k mod 7 is an isomorphism ──────────── Both power maps are bijections onto their unit groups, and the map through the exponent sends a product to a product — which is what "preserves multiplication" means, stated rather than assumed from both groups merely having six elements.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 46,656 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_lucas_numbers_follow_their_recurrence_and_reach_their_named_values">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 383</strong> (<code>the_lucas_numbers_follow_their_recurrence_and_reach_their_named_values</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_lucas_numbers_follow_their_recurrence_and_reach_their_named_values">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>lucas</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>lucas</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>lucas</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>lucas</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>29</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>29</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>lucas</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>lucas</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>lucas</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>lucas 0 = 2 ∧ lucas 1 = 1 ∧ lucas 5 = 11 ∧ lucas 7 = 29 ∧ (List.range' 2 28).all (fun n =&gt; lucas n == lucas (n - 1) + lucas (n - 2))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{lucas}\mathopen{}\left(0\right) = 2 \land \mathrm{lucas}\mathopen{}\left(1\right) = 1 \land \mathrm{lucas}\mathopen{}\left(5\right) = 11 \land \mathrm{lucas}\mathopen{}\left(7\right) = 29 \land \forall n \in \{2,\dots,29\},\; \mathrm{lucas}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) = \mathrm{lucas}\mathopen{}\left(n - 1\right) + \mathrm{lucas}\mathopen{}\left(n - 2\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the Lucas numbers: the recurrence, and the two values the row names ─────────────────────────────────</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 28 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_lucas_numbers_are_the_sum_of_the_neighbouring_fibonaccis">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 384</strong> (<code>the_lucas_numbers_are_the_sum_of_the_neighbouring_fibonaccis</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_lucas_numbers_are_the_sum_of_the_neighbouring_fibonaccis">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>28</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>lucas</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 28).all (fun n =&gt; lucas n == fib (n - 1) + fib (n + 1))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{1,\dots,28\},\; \mathrm{lucas}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) = \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(n - 1\right) + \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(n + 1\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── and Lucas is Fibonacci's neighbours added: L(n) = F(n−1) + F(n+1) ─────────────────────────────────── Two independently defined sequences meeting, which is more than either recurrence says on its own.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 28 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_pell_numbers_follow_their_recurrence_and_reach_their_named_values">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 385</strong> (<code>the_pell_numbers_follow_their_recurrence_and_reach_their_named_values</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_pell_numbers_follow_their_recurrence_and_reach_their_named_values">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>pell</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>29</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>pell</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>70</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>pell</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>pell</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>pell</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>pell 5 = 29 ∧ pell 6 = 70 ∧ (List.range' 2 24).all (fun n =&gt; pell n == 2 * pell (n - 1) + pell (n - 2))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{pell}\mathopen{}\left(5\right) = 29 \land \mathrm{pell}\mathopen{}\left(6\right) = 70 \land \forall n \in \{2,\dots,25\},\; \mathrm{pell}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) = 2 \cdot \mathrm{pell}\mathopen{}\left(n - 1\right) + \mathrm{pell}\mathopen{}\left(n - 2\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the Pell numbers: doubling recurrence, and the two values the row names ─────────────────────────────</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 24 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-consecutive_farey_neighbours_have_unit_determinant_and_bracket_their_mediant">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 386</strong> (<code>consecutive_farey_neighbours_have_unit_determinant_and_bracket_their_mediant</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_consecutive_farey_neighbours_have_unit_determinant_and_bracket_their_mediant">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range ((farey 4).length - 1)).all (fun i =&gt; let x := (farey 4).getD i (0, 1); let y := (farey 4).getD (i + 1) (0, 1) x.2 * y.1 == x.1 * y.2 + 1) ∧ (List.range ((farey 6).length - 1)).all (fun i =&gt; let x := (farey 6).getD i (0, 1); let y := (farey 6).getD (i + 1) (0, 1) let m := (x.1 + y.1, x.2 + y.2) x.1 * m.2 &lt; m.1 * x.2 &amp;&amp; m.1 * y.2 &lt; y.1 * m.2)</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_units_are_three_regular_under_doubling_halving_and_reflection">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 387</strong> (<code>the_units_are_three_regular_under_doubling_halving_and_reflection</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_units_are_three_regular_under_doubling_halving_and_reflection">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>degreeSet</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>degreeSet (unitsMod 9) = [3]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{degreeSet}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right)\right) = [3]</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── on the units the graph is regular: every unit has exactly three neighbours ──────────────────────────</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_whole_ring_is_not_regular_and_the_triad_is_why">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 388</strong> (<code>the_whole_ring_is_not_regular_and_the_triad_is_why</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_whole_ring_is_not_regular_and_the_triad_is_why">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>degreeSet</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>nbrs</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>:</mo><mrow><mi>List</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>Nat</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>nbrs</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>degreeSet (List.range 9) ≠ [3] ∧ (nbrs (List.range 9) 0).length = 0 ∧ ([3, 6] : List Nat).all (fun d =&gt; (nbrs (List.range 9) d).length == 1)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{degreeSet}\mathopen{}\left(\{0,\dots,8\}\right) \neq [3] \land \left|\mathrm{nbrs}\mathopen{}\left(\{0,\dots,8\},\,0\right)\right| = 0 \land \forall d \in \left([3,\,6] : \mathrm{List}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{Nat}\right)\right),\; \left|\mathrm{nbrs}\mathopen{}\left(\{0,\dots,8\},\,d\right)\right| = 1</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── and on the whole ring it is not, with the triad as the exact obstruction ──────────────────────────── Zero is fixed by all three maps and has no neighbours at all; three and six see only each other. The degree set has more than one element, which is the test the peer proposed, answered in the negative.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 1,458 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_interior_and_exterior_angles_are_n_straight_angles">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 389</strong> (<code>the_interior_and_exterior_angles_are_n_straight_angles</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_interior_and_exterior_angles_are_n_straight_angles">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>32</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mn>180</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>360</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mn>180</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>180</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>180</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>108</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>180</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>135</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 3 30).all (fun n =&gt; (n - 2) * 180 + 360 == n * 180) ∧ 180 * (3 - 2) / 3 = 60 ∧ 180 * (5 - 2) / 5 = 108 ∧ 180 * (8 - 2) / 8 = 135</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{3,\dots,32\},\; n - 2 \cdot 180 + 360 = n \cdot 180 \land \frac{180 \cdot 3 - 2}{3} = 60 \land \frac{180 \cdot 5 - 2}{5} = 108 \land \frac{180 \cdot 8 - 2}{8} = 135</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the exterior angles of any regular polygon sum to a full turn ─────────────────────────────────────── `geom_exterior_360` was orphaned holding `[3,5,8].all (fun n =&gt; n * (360 / n) == 360)`, which is true only because 3, 5 and 8 happen to divide 360 — a statement about integer division wearing a geometry name. The interior angles of an n-gon sum to (n−2)·180 and the exterior to 360, and together they are n straight angles. That identity needs no division and holds at every n.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 30 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-a_knight_has_exactly_eight_leaps_and_every_one_flips_the_colour">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 390</strong> (<code>a_knight_has_exactly_eight_leaps_and_every_one_flips_the_colour</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_a_knight_has_exactly_eight_leaps_and_every_one_flips_the_colour">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>knightSteps</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>dedup</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>knightSteps</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>knightSteps</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>knightSteps.length = 8 ∧ knightSteps.eraseDups.length = 8 ∧ knightSteps.all (fun p =&gt; (p.1 + p.2) % 2 == 1)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\mathrm{knightSteps}\right| = 8 \land \left|\operatorname{dedup}\left(\mathrm{knightSteps}\right)\right| = 8 \land \forall p \in \mathrm{knightSteps},\; p_{1} + p_{2} \bmod 2 = 1</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── a knight has exactly eight leaps, and every one changes the colour of its square ──────────────────── Colour is the parity of row + column, and the offsets are written as 0…4 for −2…2. |a−2| ≡ a (mod 2), so the parity of the shifted pair is the parity of the real step — the check is not an artefact of the encoding.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_golden_beatty_identity_holds_across_the_range">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 391</strong> (<code>the_golden_beatty_identity_holds_across_the_range</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_golden_beatty_identity_holds_across_the_range">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>upperWythoff</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>-</mo><mrow><mi>lowerWythoff</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 40).all (fun n =&gt; upperWythoff n - lowerWythoff n == n)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{1,\dots,40\},\; \mathrm{upperWythoff}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) - \mathrm{lowerWythoff}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) = n</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the Wythoff pair: ⌊nφ²⌋ − ⌊nφ⌋ = n, the golden Beatty identity ──────────────────────────────────────</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 40 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_wythoff_sequences_partition_the_integers">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 392</strong> (<code>the_wythoff_sequences_partition_the_integers</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_wythoff_sequences_partition_the_integers">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 50).all (fun m =&gt; ((List.range' 1 40).map lowerWythoff).count m + ((List.range' 1 40).map upperWythoff).count m == 1)</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 80,000 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_partition_and_bell_numbers_count_what_they_claim_to_count">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 393</strong> (<code>the_partition_and_bell_numbers_count_what_they_claim_to_count</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_partition_and_bell_numbers_count_what_they_claim_to_count">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>partitionsOf</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>partitionsOf</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>partitionsOf</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>42</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>rgs</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>bellOf</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>bellOf</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>bellOf</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>bellOf</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>52</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(partitionsOf 5).length = 7 ∧ (partitionsOf 7).length = 15 ∧ (partitionsOf 10).length = 42 ∧ (List.range 6).all (fun n =&gt; (rgs n).length == bellOf n) ∧ bellOf 3 = 5 ∧ bellOf 4 = 15 ∧ bellOf 5 = 52</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\mathrm{partitionsOf}\mathopen{}\left(5\right)\right| = 7 \land \left|\mathrm{partitionsOf}\mathopen{}\left(7\right)\right| = 15 \land \left|\mathrm{partitionsOf}\mathopen{}\left(10\right)\right| = 42 \land \forall n \in \{0,\dots,5\},\; \left|\mathrm{rgs}\mathopen{}\left(n\right)\right| = \mathrm{bellOf}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) \land \mathrm{bellOf}\mathopen{}\left(3\right) = 5 \land \mathrm{bellOf}\mathopen{}\left(4\right) = 15 \land \mathrm{bellOf}\mathopen{}\left(5\right) = 52</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 6 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_unit_graph_is_complete_bipartite_between_the_two_tetrahedra">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 394</strong> (<code>the_unit_graph_is_complete_bipartite_between_the_two_tetrahedra</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_unit_graph_is_complete_bipartite_between_the_two_tetrahedra">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>tetOf</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>tetOf</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>tetOf</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>nbrs</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>nbrs</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>tetOf</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>tetOf</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>nbrs</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>nbrs</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>tetOf</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>nbrs</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>nbrs</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>∨</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>nbrs</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>unitsMod</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(tetOf 1).length = 3 ∧ (tetOf 2).length = 3 ∧ (tetOf 1).all (fun d =&gt; (nbrs (unitsMod 9) d).length == 3 &amp;&amp; (nbrs (unitsMod 9) d).all (fun t =&gt; (tetOf 2).contains t)) ∧ (tetOf 2).all (fun d =&gt; (nbrs (unitsMod 9) d).length == 3 &amp;&amp; (nbrs (unitsMod 9) d).all (fun t =&gt; (tetOf 1).contains t)) ∧ (unitsMod 9).all (fun d =&gt; (nbrs (unitsMod 9) d).all (fun x =&gt; (nbrs (unitsMod 9) d).all (fun y =&gt; x == y || !((nbrs (unitsMod 9) x).contains y))))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\mathrm{tetOf}\mathopen{}\left(1\right)\right| = 3 \land \left|\mathrm{tetOf}\mathopen{}\left(2\right)\right| = 3 \land \forall d \in \mathrm{tetOf}\mathopen{}\left(1\right),\; \left|\mathrm{nbrs}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right),\,d\right)\right| = 3 \land \forall t \in \mathrm{nbrs}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right),\,d\right),\; t \in \mathrm{tetOf}\mathopen{}\left(2\right) \land \forall d \in \mathrm{tetOf}\mathopen{}\left(2\right),\; \left|\mathrm{nbrs}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right),\,d\right)\right| = 3 \land \forall t \in \mathrm{nbrs}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right),\,d\right),\; t \in \mathrm{tetOf}\mathopen{}\left(1\right) \land \forall d \in \mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right),\; \forall x \in \mathrm{nbrs}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right),\,d\right),\; \forall y \in \mathrm{nbrs}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right),\,d\right),\; x = y \lor \lnot y \in \mathrm{nbrs}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{unitsMod}\mathopen{}\left(9\right),\,x\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-eight_times_a_triangular_number_plus_one_is_an_odd_square_for_every_n">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 398</strong> (<code>eight_times_a_triangular_number_plus_one_is_an_odd_square_for_every_n</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_eight_times_a_triangular_number_plus_one_is_an_odd_square_for_every_n">sealed</a>.</p>

<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 399</strong> (<code>the_lucas_numbers_are_the_sum_of_the_neighbouring_fibonaccis_for_every_n</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_lucas_numbers_are_the_sum_of_the_neighbouring_fibonaccis_for_every_n">sealed</a>.</p>

<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_polygon_side_count_reads_back_from_its_angle_sum">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 400</strong> (<code>the_polygon_side_count_reads_back_from_its_angle_sum</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_polygon_side_count_reads_back_from_its_angle_sum">sealed</a>.</p>

<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-every_odd_square_one_more_than_eight_times_m_makes_m_triangular">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 401</strong> (<code>every_odd_square_one_more_than_eight_times_m_makes_m_triangular</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_every_odd_square_one_more_than_eight_times_m_makes_m_triangular">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ m r : Nat, 8 * m + 1 = r * r → m = r / 2 * (r / 2 + 1) / 2</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-the_fibonaccis_are_a_fifth_of_the_neighbouring_lucas_numbers_for_every_n">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 402</strong> (<code>the_fibonaccis_are_a_fifth_of_the_neighbouring_lucas_numbers_for_every_n</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_the_fibonaccis_are_a_fifth_of_the_neighbouring_lucas_numbers_for_every_n">sealed</a>.</p>

<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-elementary-half_a_product_of_consecutive_numbers_multiplies_back_for_every_n">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 403</strong> (<code>half_a_product_of_consecutive_numbers_multiplies_back_for_every_n</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_elementary_half_a_product_of_consecutive_numbers_multiplies_back_for_every_n">sealed</a>.</p>

</div>
