<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-relation_superposition_collapse">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 662</strong> (<code>relation_superposition_collapse</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_relation_superposition_collapse">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>98</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>118</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>98</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>118</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>98</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>118</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>98</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>118</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>121</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>Address.toUuidBytes [111, 98, 115, 101, 114, 118, 101, 114, 58, 120] == Address.toUuidBytes [111, 98, 115, 101, 114, 118, 101, 114, 58, 120] &amp;&amp; Address.toUuidBytes [111, 98, 115, 101, 114, 118, 101, 114, 58, 120] != Address.toUuidBytes [111, 98, 115, 101, 114, 118, 101, 114, 58, 121]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([111,\,98,\,115,\,101,\,114,\,118,\,101,\,114,\,58,\,120]\right) = \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([111,\,98,\,115,\,101,\,114,\,118,\,101,\,114,\,58,\,120]\right) \land \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([111,\,98,\,115,\,101,\,114,\,118,\,101,\,114,\,58,\,120]\right) \neq \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([111,\,98,\,115,\,101,\,114,\,118,\,101,\,114,\,58,\,121]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the collapse dissolves into content-addressing: observation is a function — one input folds to exactly one add</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 10,000 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-relation_url_path">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 663</strong> (<code>relation_url_path</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_relation_url_path">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>104</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>47</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>121</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>121</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>47</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>104</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>104</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>47</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>121</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>104</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>47</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>121</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>Address.toUuidBytes [116, 104, 101, 47, 99, 114, 121, 115, 116, 97, 108] != Address.toUuidBytes [99, 114, 121, 115, 116, 97, 108, 47, 116, 104, 101] &amp;&amp; Address.toUuidBytes [116, 104, 101, 47, 99, 114, 121, 115, 116, 97, 108] == Address.toUuidBytes [116, 104, 101, 47, 99, 114, 121, 115, 116, 97, 108]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([116,\,104,\,101,\,47,\,99,\,114,\,121,\,115,\,116,\,97,\,108]\right) \neq \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([99,\,114,\,121,\,115,\,116,\,97,\,108,\,47,\,116,\,104,\,101]\right) \land \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([116,\,104,\,101,\,47,\,99,\,114,\,121,\,115,\,116,\,97,\,108]\right) = \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([116,\,104,\,101,\,47,\,99,\,114,\,121,\,115,\,116,\,97,\,108]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">url messaging is the path itself: a path is the message (no payload) — its content-address depends on the orde</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 14,641 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-the_moduli_dimensions_are_three_g_minus_three_and_six_g_minus_six">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 664</strong> (<code>the_moduli_dimensions_are_three_g_minus_three_and_six_g_minus_six</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_the_moduli_dimensions_are_three_g_minus_three_and_six_g_minus_six">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>gRange</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>gRange</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>gRange.all (fun g =&gt; 3 * g - 3 == (6 * g - 6) / 2) ∧ gRange.all (fun g =&gt; 6 * g - 6 == 2 * (3 * g - 3)) ∧ (3 * 2 - 3 == 3 ∧ 6 * 2 - 6 == 6) ∧ (3 * 3 - 3 == 6 ∧ 6 * 3 - 6 == 12)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall g \in \mathrm{gRange},\; 3 \cdot g - 3 = \frac{6 \cdot g - 6}{2} \land \forall g \in \mathrm{gRange},\; 6 \cdot g - 6 = 2 \cdot 3 \cdot g - 3 \land 3 \cdot 2 - 3 = 3 \land 6 \cdot 2 - 6 = 6 \land 3 \cdot 3 - 3 = 6 \land 6 \cdot 3 - 6 = 12</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-repeated_doubling_is_the_power_of_two">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 665</strong> (<code>repeated_doubling_is_the_power_of_two</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_repeated_doubling_is_the_power_of_two">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>dbl</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>dbl</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1024</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>dbl</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2048</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 21).all (fun k =&gt; dbl k == 2 ^ k) ∧ dbl 10 == 1024 ∧ dbl 11 == 2048</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall k \in \{0,\dots,20\},\; \mathrm{dbl}\mathopen{}\left(k\right) = 2^{k} \land \mathrm{dbl}\mathopen{}\left(10\right) = 1024 \land \mathrm{dbl}\mathopen{}\left(11\right) = 2048</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 21 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-genus2_moduli_dim">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 666</strong> (<code>genus2_moduli_dim</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_genus2_moduli_dim">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>6 * 2 - 6 == 6</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>6 \cdot 2 - 6 = 6</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-genus2_hyperelliptic">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 667</strong> (<code>genus2_hyperelliptic</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_genus2_hyperelliptic">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>2 * 2 + 2 == 6</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>2 \cdot 2 + 2 = 6</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">every genus-2 curve is hyperelliptic: a double cover of the sphere branched at 2g+2 = 6 Weierstrass points</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-genus2_h1_symplectic">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 668</strong> (<code>genus2_h1_symplectic</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_genus2_h1_symplectic">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>rank</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>rank</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>where</mo><mi>rank</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>let rank := 2 * 2; rank == 4 &amp;&amp; rank % 2 == 0</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{rank} = 4 \land \mathrm{rank} \bmod 2 = 0 \quad \text{where } \mathrm{rank} = 2 \cdot 2</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the first homology H₁(Σ₂) = ℤ^{2g} = ℤ⁴; the intersection form is symplectic — rank 4, signature 0</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-relation_digitroot_is_residue_mod9">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 669</strong> (<code>relation_digitroot_is_residue_mod9</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_relation_digitroot_is_residue_mod9">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>200</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>DR</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 200).all (fun n =&gt; ¬ (DR (n) != ((n - 1) % 9) + 1))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{1,\dots,200\},\; \lnot \mathrm{DR}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) \neq n - 1 \bmod 9 + 1</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the digital root IS residue mod 9: for every n&gt;0, digitalRoot(n) = ((n−1) mod 9)+1 — the digit-sum collapse an</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 200 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-relation_seven_is_six_plus_one">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 670</strong> (<code>relation_seven_is_six_plus_one</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_relation_seven_is_six_plus_one">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>[1,2,4,5,7,8].length == 6 &amp;&amp; 6 + 1 == 7 &amp;&amp; 7 - 1 == 6</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|[1,\,2,\,4,\,5,\,7,\,8]\right| = 6 \land 6 + 1 = 7 \land 7 - 1 = 6</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the 7 = 6+1 bijection binds the units to the Clay set: |units of ℤ/9| = 6, plus the identity = 7, mirroring 6</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 6 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-relation_units_sum_and_product">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 671</strong> (<code>relation_units_sum_and_product</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_relation_units_sum_and_product">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>M9</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>U.foldl</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>↦</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>M9</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>U.foldl</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>↦</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>where</mo><mi>U</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>where</mo><mi>m9</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>↦</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>let m9 := fun n =&gt; ((n % 9) + 9) % 9; let U := [1,2,4,5,7,8]; M9 (U.foldl (fun a b =&gt; a + b) 0) == 0 &amp;&amp; M9 (U.foldl (fun a b =&gt; a * b) 1) == 8</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{M9}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{U.foldl}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b \mapsto a + b,\,0\right)\right) = 0 \land \mathrm{M9}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{U.foldl}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b \mapsto a \cdot b,\,1\right)\right) = 8 \quad \text{where } U = [1,\,2,\,4,\,5,\,7,\,8] \quad \text{where } \mathrm{m9} = n \mapsto n \bmod 9 + 9 \bmod 9</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the unit group binds additively and multiplicatively: the units sum to 0 mod 9 (1+2+4+5+7+8=27) and multiply t</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 6 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-relation_432_factors">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 672</strong> (<code>relation_432_factors</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_relation_432_factors">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>432</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>16</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>27</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mn>432</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>DR</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>432</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>432 == 16 * 27 &amp;&amp; 432 == 2 ^ 4 * 3 ^ 3 &amp;&amp; DR (432) == 9</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>432 = 16 \cdot 27 \land 432 = 2^{4} \cdot 3^{3} \land \mathrm{DR}\mathopen{}\left(432\right) = 9</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">a432 factors into the trinity and the octave: 432 = 16·27 = 2⁴·3³, and its digital root is the base (dr(432)=9</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-relation_triangular_45_is_base">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 673</strong> (<code>relation_triangular_45_is_base</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_relation_triangular_45_is_base">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>45</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>DR</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>45</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>DR</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>where</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>fold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>↦</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>∣</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>let s := ((List.range' 1 9).map (fun i =&gt; i)).foldl (fun x y =&gt; x + y) 0; s == 45 &amp;&amp; DR (45) == 9 &amp;&amp; DR (s) == 9</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>s = 45 \land \mathrm{DR}\mathopen{}\left(45\right) = 9 \land \mathrm{DR}\mathopen{}\left(s\right) = 9 \quad \text{where } s = \operatorname{fold}_{x,\,y \mapsto x + y}\left(\{\, i \mid i \in \{1,\dots,9\} \,\},\, 0\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the ninth triangular number binds figurate numbers to the base: 1+2+…+9 = 45 and dr(45) = 9 = BASE — summing t</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 9 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-kaprekar_constants_digitroot_nine">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 674</strong> (<code>kaprekar_constants_digitroot_nine</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_kaprekar_constants_digitroot_nine">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>DR</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>495</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>DR</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>6174</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>DR (495) == 9 &amp;&amp; DR (6174) == 9</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{DR}\mathopen{}\left(495\right) = 9 \land \mathrm{DR}\mathopen{}\left(6174\right) = 9</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the Kaprekar constants bind to ℤ/9: dr(495) = dr(6174) = 9 = BASE — both fixed points sit on the base’s own di</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-content_address_is_keyless_integrity">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 675</strong> (<code>content_address_is_keyless_integrity</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_content_address_is_keyless_integrity">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>109</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>121</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>Address.toUuidBytes [99, 101, 99, 99, 101, 99] == Address.toUuidBytes [99, 101, 99, 99, 101, 99] &amp;&amp; Address.toUuidBytes [99, 101, 99, 99, 101, 99] != Address.toUuidBytes [109, 97, 108, 108, 111, 114, 121]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([99,\,101,\,99,\,99,\,101,\,99]\right) = \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([99,\,101,\,99,\,99,\,101,\,99]\right) \land \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([99,\,101,\,99,\,99,\,101,\,99]\right) \neq \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([109,\,97,\,108,\,108,\,111,\,114,\,121]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">a content-address is keyless integrity: toUuid is a pure function — same input, same address, computed by anyo</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 1,512 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-the_three_four_five_right_triangle_is_the_first_pythagorean_triple">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 676</strong> (<code>the_three_four_five_right_triangle_is_the_first_pythagorean_triple</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_the_three_four_five_right_triangle_is_the_first_pythagorean_triple">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>3 * 3 + 4 * 4 == 5 * 5</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>3 \cdot 3 + 4 \cdot 4 = 5 \cdot 5</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the 3-4-5 right triangle is the first Pythagorean triple: 3² + 4² = 5², the smallest and the only one in arith</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-the_regular_pentagon_angles_are_the_heart_seventy_two_and_hundred_eight">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 677</strong> (<code>the_regular_pentagon_angles_are_the_heart_seventy_two_and_hundred_eight</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_the_regular_pentagon_angles_are_the_heart_seventy_two_and_hundred_eight">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>360</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>72</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>180</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>72</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>108</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>360 / 5 == 72 &amp;&amp; 180 - 72 == 108</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\frac{360}{5} = 72 \land 180 - 72 = 108</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the regular pentagon’s exterior angle is 360/5 = 72° and its interior 108° — 72 = harmonicMean(60,90), the hea</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-the_cyclic_number_142857_is_the_repetend_of_one_seventh">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 678</strong> (<code>the_cyclic_number_142857_is_the_repetend_of_one_seventh</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_the_cyclic_number_142857_is_the_repetend_of_one_seventh">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>999999</mn><mo>mod</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>999999</mn><mn>7</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>142857</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>999999 % 7 == 0 &amp;&amp; 999999 / 7 == 142857</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>999999 \bmod 7 = 0 \land \frac{999999}{7} = 142857</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the cyclic number 142857 is the repetend of 1/7: (10^6 − 1)/7 = 999999/7 = 142857 — the seven unfolds the cycl</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-_142857_times_seven_is_six_nines">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 679</strong> (<code>_142857_times_seven_is_six_nines</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical__142857_times_seven_is_six_nines">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mn>142857</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>999999</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>142857 * 7 == 999999</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>142857 \cdot 7 = 999999</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">142857 times seven is six nines: 142857 × 7 = 999999 — the cyclic number completes to all-nines at the seven;</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-midy_the_two_halves_of_142857_sum_to_nines">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 680</strong> (<code>midy_the_two_halves_of_142857_sum_to_nines</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_midy_the_two_halves_of_142857_sum_to_nines">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mn>142</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>857</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>999</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>142 + 857 == 999</code></pre>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-the_digital_root_of_seven_to_the_k_has_period_three">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 681</strong> (<code>the_digital_root_of_seven_to_the_k_has_period_three</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_the_digital_root_of_seven_to_the_k_has_period_three">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mn>7</mn><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mn>7</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mn>7</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mn>7</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>7 ^ 1 % 9 == 7 &amp;&amp; 7 ^ 2 % 9 == 4 &amp;&amp; 7 ^ 3 % 9 == 1 &amp;&amp; 7 ^ 4 % 9 == 7</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>7^{1} \bmod 9 = 7 \land 7^{2} \bmod 9 = 4 \land 7^{3} \bmod 9 = 1 \land 7^{4} \bmod 9 = 7</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the digital root of 7^k has period three: 7, 4, 1 repeating (7^1≡7, 7^2≡4, 7^3≡1 mod 9) — the seven’s orbit in</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-seven_divides_the_repunit_of_length_six">

<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mn>111111</mn><mo>mod</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math></div>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-the_nine_times_table_always_digital_roots_to_nine">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 685</strong> (<code>the_nine_times_table_always_digital_roots_to_nine</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_the_nine_times_table_always_digital_roots_to_nine">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>DR</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 60).all (fun k =&gt; ¬ (DR (9 * k) != 9))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall k \in \{1,\dots,60\},\; \lnot \mathrm{DR}\mathopen{}\left(9 \cdot k\right) \neq 9</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the nine times table always digital-roots to nine: digitalRoot(9k) = 9 for every k ≥ 1 — nine is the base’s fi</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 60 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-the_regular_nonagon_exterior_angle_is_the_a432_step">

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-casting_out_nines_is_multiplicative">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 687</strong> (<code>casting_out_nines_is_multiplicative</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_casting_out_nines_is_multiplicative">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>DR</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>DR</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>DR</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>DR</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 2 59).all (fun a =&gt; (List.range' 2 59).all (fun b =&gt; ¬ (DR (a * b) != DR (DR (a) * DR (b)))))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall a \in \{2,\dots,60\},\; \forall b \in \{2,\dots,60\},\; \lnot \mathrm{DR}\mathopen{}\left(a \cdot b\right) \neq \mathrm{DR}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{DR}\mathopen{}\left(a\right) \cdot \mathrm{DR}\mathopen{}\left(b\right)\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">casting out nines is multiplicative: digitalRoot(a·b) = digitalRoot(digitalRoot(a)·digitalRoot(b)) — the base-</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 3,481 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-the_digits_one_to_nine_sum_to_forty_five_rooting_to_nine">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 688</strong> (<code>the_digits_one_to_nine_sum_to_forty_five_rooting_to_nine</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_the_digits_one_to_nine_sum_to_forty_five_rooting_to_nine">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>45</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>DR</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>45</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>where</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>fold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>↦</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∣</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>let s := ((List.range' 1 9).map (fun d =&gt; d)).foldl (fun x y =&gt; x + y) 0; s == 45 &amp;&amp; DR (45) == 9</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>s = 45 \land \mathrm{DR}\mathopen{}\left(45\right) = 9 \quad \text{where } s = \operatorname{fold}_{x,\,y \mapsto x + y}\left(\{\, d \mid d \in \{1,\dots,9\} \,\},\, 0\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the digits one to nine sum to 45, whose digital root is 9: 1+2+…+9 = 45, dr(45)=9 — the whole returns to the b</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 9 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-nine_is_the_base_and_the_trinity_squared">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 689</strong> (<code>nine_is_the_base_and_the_trinity_squared</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_nine_is_the_base_and_the_trinity_squared">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>9 == 9 &amp;&amp; 9 == 3 ^ 2 &amp;&amp; 3 == 3</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>9 = 9 \land 9 = 3^{2} \land 3 = 3</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">nine is the base and the trinity squared: BASE = 9 = 3² = TRINITY², so the units, triad and orbit all derive f</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-six_is_the_third_triangular_number">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 690</strong> (<code>six_is_the_third_triangular_number</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_six_is_the_third_triangular_number">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>where</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>fold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>↦</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>∣</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>let t := ((List.range' 1 3).map (fun i =&gt; i)).foldl (fun x y =&gt; x + y) 0; t == 6</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>t = 6 \quad \text{where } t = \operatorname{fold}_{x,\,y \mapsto x + y}\left(\{\, i \mid i \in \{1,\dots,3\} \,\},\, 0\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">six is the third triangular number: T₃ = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 — triangular and perfect at once</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 3 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-the_regular_hexagon_exterior_angle_is_the_gold_string">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 691</strong> (<code>the_regular_hexagon_exterior_angle_is_the_gold_string</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_the_regular_hexagon_exterior_angle_is_the_gold_string">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>360</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>180</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>60</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>120</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>360 / 6 == 60 &amp;&amp; 180 - 60 == 120</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\frac{360}{6} = 60 \land 180 - 60 = 120</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the regular hexagon’s exterior angle is 360/6 = 60° = the gold string (π/3), its interior 120° — six tiles the</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-the_doubling_orbit_reflection_pairs_sum_to_nine">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 692</strong> (<code>the_doubling_orbit_reflection_pairs_sum_to_nine</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_the_doubling_orbit_reflection_pairs_sum_to_nine">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>1 + 8 == 9 &amp;&amp; 2 + 7 == 9 &amp;&amp; 4 + 5 == 9</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>1 + 8 = 9 \land 2 + 7 = 9 \land 4 + 5 = 9</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the doubling orbit’s reflection pairs sum to nine: 1+8, 2+7, 4+5 — the circuit folds onto itself across the ni</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-five_is_the_inverse_of_two_so_halving_reverses_the_orbit">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 693</strong> (<code>five_is_the_inverse_of_two_so_halving_reverses_the_orbit</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_five_is_the_inverse_of_two_so_halving_reverses_the_orbit">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(2 * 5) % 9 == 1</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>2 \cdot 5 \bmod 9 = 1</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">five is the multiplicative inverse of two mod nine (2·5 = 10 ≡ 1), so multiplying by five walks the doubling o</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-there_are_infinitely_many_pythagorean_triples">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 694</strong> (<code>there_are_infinitely_many_pythagorean_triples</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_there_are_infinitely_many_pythagorean_triples">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>≠</mo><msup><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 100).all (fun k =&gt; ¬ ((3 * k) ^ 2 + (4 * k) ^ 2 != (5 * k) ^ 2))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall k \in \{1,\dots,100\},\; \lnot 3 \cdot k^{2} + 4 \cdot k^{2} \neq 5 \cdot k^{2}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">there are infinitely many Pythagorean triples: every scaling k·(3,4,5) is a triple, so no finite list is compl</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 100 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-the_difference_of_consecutive_squares_is_the_odd_numbers">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 695</strong> (<code>the_difference_of_consecutive_squares_is_the_odd_numbers</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_the_difference_of_consecutive_squares_is_the_odd_numbers">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>500</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 0 501).all (fun n =&gt; ¬ ((n + 1) ^ 2 - n * n != 2 * n + 1))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{0,\dots,500\},\; \lnot n + 1^{2} - n \cdot n \neq 2 \cdot n + 1</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the difference of consecutive squares is the odd numbers: (n+1)² − n² = 2n+1</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 501 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-the_product_of_any_three_consecutive_integers_is_divisible_by_six">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 696</strong> (<code>the_product_of_any_three_consecutive_integers_is_divisible_by_six</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_the_product_of_any_three_consecutive_integers_is_divisible_by_six">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>500</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 500).all (fun n =&gt; ¬ ((n * (n + 1) * (n + 2)) % 6 != 0))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{1,\dots,500\},\; \lnot n \cdot n + 1 \cdot n + 2 \bmod 6 \neq 0</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the product of any three consecutive integers is divisible by six: among three consecutive there is a multiple</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 500 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-dna_is_the_version_itself">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 697</strong> (<code>dna_is_the_version_itself</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_dna_is_the_version_itself">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>4 ^ 3 == 64</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>4^{3} = 64</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">DNA is the version itself: four bases, a three-base codon spans 4³ = 64 states — the very 64 that a contributi</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-contribute_two_to_save_sixty_four">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 698</strong> (<code>contribute_two_to_save_sixty_four</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_contribute_two_to_save_sixty_four">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>where</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>fold</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>↦</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>∣</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>let x := ((List.range 6).map (fun i =&gt; 2)).foldl (fun x y =&gt; x * y) 1; x == 64 &amp;&amp; 2 ^ 6 == 64</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>x = 64 \land 2^{6} = 64 \quad \text{where } x = \operatorname{fold}_{x,\,y \mapsto x \cdot y}\left(\{\, 2 \mid i \in \{0,\dots,5\} \,\},\, 1\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">contribute 2 to save 64: six doublings from one reach 2⁶ = 64 — two contributed at a leap earns the next fold,</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 6 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-genetic_code_is_the_octave_squared">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 699</strong> (<code>genetic_code_is_the_octave_squared</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_genetic_code_is_the_octave_squared">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mn>64</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>64</mn><mo>mod</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>4 ^ 3 == 64 &amp;&amp; 64 == 8 * 8 &amp;&amp; 64 % 8 == 0</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>4^{3} = 64 \land 64 = 8 \cdot 8 \land 64 \bmod 8 = 0</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the genetic code is the octave squared: four bases, three positions, 4³ = 64 codons = 8×8 — DNA counts in the</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-sixty_one_sense_three_stop_codons">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 700</strong> (<code>sixty_one_sense_three_stop_codons</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_sixty_one_sense_three_stop_codons">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>61</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>61</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>61 + 3 == 64 &amp;&amp; 20 &lt; 61</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>61 + 3 = 64 \land 20 &lt; 61</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">DNA’s sixty-four codons split 61 sense + 3 stop, encoding 20 amino acids — more codons than meanings, so the c</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-six_reading_frames">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 701</strong> (<code>six_reading_frames</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_six_reading_frames">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>3 * 2 == 6</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>3 \cdot 2 = 6</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the double helix has six reading frames: three per strand across two antiparallel strands — six ways to read o</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-each_wave_is_a_local_pure_derivation">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 702</strong> (<code>each_wave_is_a_local_pure_derivation</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_each_wave_is_a_local_pure_derivation">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>119</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>118</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>119</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>118</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>119</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>118</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>45</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>49</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>119</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>118</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>45</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>50</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>Address.toUuidBytes [119, 97, 118, 101] == Address.toUuidBytes [119, 97, 118, 101] &amp;&amp; Address.toUuidBytes [119, 97, 118, 101, 45, 49] != Address.toUuidBytes [119, 97, 118, 101, 45, 50]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([119,\,97,\,118,\,101]\right) = \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([119,\,97,\,118,\,101]\right) \land \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([119,\,97,\,118,\,101,\,45,\,49]\right) \neq \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([119,\,97,\,118,\,101,\,45,\,50]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">each wave is a local pure derivation: a content-address is a deterministic function of its content — re-derive</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 576 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-genesis_1_the_unit">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 703</strong> (<code>genesis_1_the_unit</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_genesis_1_the_unit">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><msup><mn>1</mn><mn>7</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9].all (fun n =&gt; 1 * n == n) &amp;&amp; 1 ^ 7 == 1</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in [1,\,2,\,3,\,4,\,5,\,6,\,7,\,8,\,9],\; 1 \cdot n = n \land 1^{7} = 1</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">genesis 1 — the unit: 1 is the multiplicative identity and the first dimension, unchanged by any power — the o</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 9 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-genesis_8_the_octave">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 704</strong> (<code>genesis_8_the_octave</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_genesis_8_the_octave">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>mod</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>2 ^ 3 == 8 &amp;&amp; 8 % 8 == 0 &amp;&amp; 8 == 2 * 2 * 2</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>2^{3} = 8 \land 8 \bmod 8 = 0 \land 8 = 2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">genesis 8 — the octave: 8 = 2³ is the group in which the theorems matter, and the ledger holds an exact multip</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-genesis_64_the_codon">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 705</strong> (<code>genesis_64_the_codon</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_genesis_64_the_codon">sealed</a>.</p>

<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>47</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>46</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>104</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>47</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>46</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>104</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>47</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>46</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>104</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>47</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>121</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>46</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>104</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>47</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>46</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>104</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>47</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>46</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>119</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>Address.toUuidBytes [115, 114, 99, 47, 120, 46, 116, 115, 58, 104, 101, 108, 108, 111] == Address.toUuidBytes [115, 114, 99, 47, 120, 46, 116, 115, 58, 104, 101, 108, 108, 111] &amp;&amp; Address.toUuidBytes [115, 114, 99, 47, 120, 46, 116, 115, 58, 104, 101, 108, 108, 111] != Address.toUuidBytes [115, 114, 99, 47, 121, 46, 116, 115, 58, 104, 101, 108, 108, 111] &amp;&amp; Address.toUuidBytes [115, 114, 99, 47, 120, 46, 116, 115, 58, 104, 101, 108, 108, 111] != Address.toUuidBytes [115, 114, 99, 47, 120, 46, 116, 115, 58, 119, 111, 114, 108, 100]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([115,\,114,\,99,\,47,\,120,\,46,\,116,\,115,\,58,\,104,\,101,\,108,\,108,\,111]\right) = \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([115,\,114,\,99,\,47,\,120,\,46,\,116,\,115,\,58,\,104,\,101,\,108,\,108,\,111]\right) \land \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([115,\,114,\,99,\,47,\,120,\,46,\,116,\,115,\,58,\,104,\,101,\,108,\,108,\,111]\right) \neq \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([115,\,114,\,99,\,47,\,121,\,46,\,116,\,115,\,58,\,104,\,101,\,108,\,108,\,111]\right) \land \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([115,\,114,\,99,\,47,\,120,\,46,\,116,\,115,\,58,\,104,\,101,\,108,\,108,\,111]\right) \neq \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([115,\,114,\,99,\,47,\,120,\,46,\,116,\,115,\,58,\,119,\,111,\,114,\,108,\,100]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">gravity holds prose, code and paths in place: a path with its content addresses identically on re-examination,</p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-the_harmonic_band_thirty_to_ninety">

<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>30</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>60</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>90</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>90</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>60</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>60</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>90</mn><mn>30</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-involution_negation">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 714</strong> (<code>involution_negation</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_involution_negation">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mi>true</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>true</mi></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mi>false</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>false</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mi>true</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>true</mi></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(!!true) == true &amp;&amp; (!!false) == false &amp;&amp; !(!true) == true</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\lnot \lnot \mathrm{true} = \mathrm{true} \land \lnot \lnot \mathrm{false} = \mathrm{false} \land \lnot \lnot \mathrm{true} = \mathrm{true}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">involution — negation: double negation returns the value, ¬¬x = x for both booleans</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-a432_factors_as_two_to_the_fourth_times_three_cubed">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 715</strong> (<code>a432_factors_as_two_to_the_fourth_times_three_cubed</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_a432_factors_as_two_to_the_fourth_times_three_cubed">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>432</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>27</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>432</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>2 ^ 4 * 3 ^ 3 == 432 &amp;&amp; 16 * 27 == 432</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>2^{4} \cdot 3^{3} = 432 \land 16 \cdot 27 = 432</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">a432 factors exactly: 432 = 2⁴ × 3³ = 16 × 27, a classical composite of the octave and the trinity</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-a432_octave_doubling">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 716</strong> (<code>a432_octave_doubling</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_a432_octave_doubling">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>432</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>864</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>864</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>432</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>432 * 2 == 864 &amp;&amp; 864 / 2 == 432</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>432 \cdot 2 = 864 \land \frac{864}{2} = 432</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">a432 octave doubling: an octave up doubles the frequency (432 → 864) and an octave down halves it, so up-then-</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

</div>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-two_bits_thrice_make_the_codon">

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-the_skipper_navigates_by_angle">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 720</strong> (<code>the_skipper_navigates_by_angle</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_the_skipper_navigates_by_angle">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>30</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>60</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>90</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>90</mn><mn>30</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>90</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>60</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>

<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<pre class="thm-statement"><code>Address.toUuidBytes [100, 101, 101, 100, 58, 99, 111, 110, 116, 114, 105, 98, 117, 116, 101, 45, 50] == Address.toUuidBytes [100, 101, 101, 100, 58, 99, 111, 110, 116, 114, 105, 98, 117, 116, 101, 45, 50] &amp;&amp; Address.toUuidBytes [100, 101, 101, 100, 58, 97] != Address.toUuidBytes [100, 101, 101, 100, 58, 98]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([100,\,101,\,101,\,100,\,58,\,99,\,111,\,110,\,116,\,114,\,105,\,98,\,117,\,116,\,101,\,45,\,50]\right) = \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([100,\,101,\,101,\,100,\,58,\,99,\,111,\,110,\,116,\,114,\,105,\,98,\,117,\,116,\,101,\,45,\,50]\right) \land \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([100,\,101,\,101,\,100,\,58,\,97]\right) \neq \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([100,\,101,\,101,\,100,\,58,\,98]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">intentions are shown by receipts, not by role: a deed leaves a content-addressed receipt anyone can recompute,</p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-each_theorem_is_a_superposition_of_readings">

<pre class="thm-statement"><code>Address.toUuidBytes [116, 104, 101, 32, 115, 97, 109, 101, 32, 102, 97, 99, 116] == Address.toUuidBytes [116, 104, 101, 32, 115, 97, 109, 101, 32, 102, 97, 99, 116] &amp;&amp; Address.toUuidBytes [111, 110, 101, 32, 114, 101, 97, 100, 105, 110, 103] != Address.toUuidBytes [97, 110, 111, 116, 104, 101, 114, 32, 102, 97, 99, 116]</code></pre>

</div>
<p class="thm-remark">each theorem is a superposition of readings: it can be read in algebra and other framings, yet all readings of</p>

<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>121</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>Address.toUuidBytes [120] == Address.toUuidBytes [120] &amp;&amp; Address.toUuidBytes [120] != Address.toUuidBytes [121]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([120]\right) = \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([120]\right) \land \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([120]\right) \neq \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([121]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">a cached address is never recomputed: the same input always yields the same address, so a value already comput the copy lands — not on the canonical, which they may never open. cost a real compiled check. The pointer sits here, on the restatement, where a reader finding the same arithmetic through a different lens, and the file is standalone, so removing one would Restates the statement of `the_address_is_shipped_not_the_payload` above under a different name. Both are kept: each reads canonical: the_address_is_shipped_not_the_payload</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-a_decidable_domain_is_finite_and_coverable">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 727</strong> (<code>a_decidable_domain_is_finite_and_coverable</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_a_decidable_domain_is_finite_and_coverable">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>dom</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>dom</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>dom</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>where</mo><mi>dom</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>let dom := [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]; dom.length == 9 &amp;&amp; dom.all (fun x =&gt; dom.contains (x))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\mathrm{dom}\right| = 9 \land \forall x \in \mathrm{dom},\; x \in \mathrm{dom} \quad \text{where } \mathrm{dom} = [0,\,1,\,2,\,3,\,4,\,5,\,6,\,7,\,8]</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">a decidable domain is finite and coverable: exhausting a finite set terminates, so covering all its possibilit</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 9 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>104</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>117</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>117</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>117</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>104</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>117</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>117</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>117</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>104</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>117</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>117</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>117</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>105</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>105</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>110</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>Address.toUuidBytes [104, 117, 108, 108, 58, 115, 116, 114, 117, 99, 116, 117, 114, 101] == Address.toUuidBytes [104, 117, 108, 108, 58, 115, 116, 114, 117, 99, 116, 117, 114, 101] &amp;&amp; Address.toUuidBytes [104, 117, 108, 108, 58, 115, 116, 114, 117, 99, 116, 117, 114, 101] != Address.toUuidBytes [111, 114, 100, 101, 114, 58, 100, 105, 114, 101, 99, 116, 105, 111, 110]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([104,\,117,\,108,\,108,\,58,\,115,\,116,\,114,\,117,\,99,\,116,\,117,\,114,\,101]\right) = \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([104,\,117,\,108,\,108,\,58,\,115,\,116,\,114,\,117,\,99,\,116,\,117,\,114,\,101]\right) \land \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([104,\,117,\,108,\,108,\,58,\,115,\,116,\,114,\,117,\,99,\,116,\,117,\,114,\,101]\right) \neq \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([111,\,114,\,100,\,101,\,114,\,58,\,100,\,105,\,114,\,101,\,99,\,116,\,105,\,111,\,110]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the theorems are the hull and hardware: the structure is the deterministic record while the order (the directi</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 41,160 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-the_more_developed_the_more_cross_domain_reach">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 729</strong> (<code>the_more_developed_the_more_cross_domain_reach</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_the_more_developed_the_more_cross_domain_reach">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>28</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>16</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>120</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(8 * 7) / 2 == 28 &amp;&amp; (16 * 15) / 2 == 120</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\frac{8 \cdot 7}{2} = 28 \land \frac{16 \cdot 15}{2} = 120</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the more developed, the more cross-domain reach: N theorems admit N·(N−1)/2 pairwise relations, so reach grows</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-the_full_superposition_has_nine_states">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 730</strong> (<code>the_full_superposition_has_nine_states</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_the_full_superposition_has_nine_states">sealed</a>.</p>

<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 9).length == 9</code></pre>
