<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>119</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>110</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>47</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>119</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>110</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>47</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>119</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>110</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>Address.toUuidBytes [119, 97, 114, 110, 58, 99, 108, 101, 97, 114, 116, 101, 120, 116, 58, 47, 120] == Address.toUuidBytes [119, 97, 114, 110, 58, 99, 108, 101, 97, 114, 116, 101, 120, 116, 58, 47, 120] &amp;&amp; Address.toUuidBytes [119, 97, 114, 110, 58, 120] != Address.toUuidBytes [101, 114, 114, 111, 114, 58, 120]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([119,\,97,\,114,\,110,\,58,\,99,\,108,\,101,\,97,\,114,\,116,\,101,\,120,\,116,\,58,\,47,\,120]\right) = \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([119,\,97,\,114,\,110,\,58,\,99,\,108,\,101,\,97,\,114,\,116,\,101,\,120,\,116,\,58,\,47,\,120]\right) \land \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([119,\,97,\,114,\,110,\,58,\,120]\right) \neq \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([101,\,114,\,114,\,111,\,114,\,58,\,120]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">every warning is a receipted trial event: a warning maps to a content-addressed event distinct from an error,</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 12,138 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-a_content_address_detects_any_change">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 735</strong> (<code>a_content_address_detects_any_change</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_a_content_address_detects_any_change">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>65</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>84</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>Address.toUuidBytes [100, 97, 116, 97] != Address.toUuidBytes [100, 65, 84, 97] &amp;&amp; Address.toUuidBytes [100, 97, 116, 97] == Address.toUuidBytes [100, 97, 116, 97]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([100,\,97,\,116,\,97]\right) \neq \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([100,\,65,\,84,\,97]\right) \land \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([100,\,97,\,116,\,97]\right) = \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([100,\,97,\,116,\,97]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">a content-address detects any change: altering a single character changes the address, so any corruption is de</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 256 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-a_sensor_reading_addresses_to_a_uuid">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 736</strong> (<code>a_sensor_reading_addresses_to_a_uuid</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_a_sensor_reading_addresses_to_a_uuid">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>109</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>112</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>50</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>49</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>46</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>52</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>109</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>112</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>50</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>49</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>46</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>52</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>109</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>112</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>50</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>49</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>46</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>52</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>109</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>112</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>50</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>49</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>46</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>53</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>Address.toUuidBytes [116, 101, 109, 112, 58, 50, 49, 46, 52] == Address.toUuidBytes [116, 101, 109, 112, 58, 50, 49, 46, 52] &amp;&amp; Address.toUuidBytes [116, 101, 109, 112, 58, 50, 49, 46, 52] != Address.toUuidBytes [116, 101, 109, 112, 58, 50, 49, 46, 53]</code></pre>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-forward_is_the_deterministic_compute">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 737</strong> (<code>forward_is_the_deterministic_compute</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_forward_is_the_deterministic_compute">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>98</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>Address.toUuidBytes [120] == Address.toUuidBytes [120] &amp;&amp; Address.toUuidBytes [97] != Address.toUuidBytes [98]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([120]\right) = \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([120]\right) \land \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([97]\right) \neq \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([98]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">forward is the deterministic compute: addressing a value forward gives the same result every time — the forwar</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-the_fusion_of_site_and_user_is_deterministic">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 738</strong> (<code>the_fusion_of_site_and_user_is_deterministic</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_the_fusion_of_site_and_user_is_deterministic">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>105</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>64</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>98</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>103</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>105</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>64</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>98</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>103</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>105</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>64</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>98</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>103</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>115</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>105</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>64</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>Address.toUuidBytes [115, 105, 116, 101, 64, 98, 103] == Address.toUuidBytes [115, 105, 116, 101, 64, 98, 103] &amp;&amp; Address.toUuidBytes [115, 105, 116, 101, 64, 98, 103] != Address.toUuidBytes [115, 105, 116, 101, 64, 100, 101]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([115,\,105,\,116,\,101,\,64,\,98,\,103]\right) = \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([115,\,105,\,116,\,101,\,64,\,98,\,103]\right) \land \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([115,\,105,\,116,\,101,\,64,\,98,\,103]\right) \neq \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([115,\,105,\,116,\,101,\,64,\,100,\,101]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the fusion of site and user is deterministic: site plus user resolves to one reproducible view</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 2,401 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-each_suggested_next_is_content_addressed">

<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>47</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>104</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>109</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>47</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>47</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>104</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>109</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>47</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>47</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>104</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>109</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>47</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>47</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>104</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>109</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>47</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>Address.toUuidBytes [47, 116, 104, 101, 111, 114, 101, 109, 47, 97] == Address.toUuidBytes [47, 116, 104, 101, 111, 114, 101, 109, 47, 97] &amp;&amp; Address.toUuidBytes [47, 116, 104, 101, 111, 114, 101, 109, 47, 97] != Address.toUuidBytes [47, 116, 104, 101, 111, 114, 101, 109, 47, 99]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([47,\,116,\,104,\,101,\,111,\,114,\,101,\,109,\,47,\,97]\right) = \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([47,\,116,\,104,\,101,\,111,\,114,\,101,\,109,\,47,\,97]\right) \land \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([47,\,116,\,104,\,101,\,111,\,114,\,101,\,109,\,47,\,97]\right) \neq \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([47,\,116,\,104,\,101,\,111,\,114,\,101,\,109,\,47,\,99]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">each suggested next is content-addressed: every suggestion resolves to a deterministic link to its page, so th</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 10,000 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-the_rejected_command_gets_a_receipt">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 740</strong> (<code>the_rejected_command_gets_a_receipt</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_the_rejected_command_gets_a_receipt">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>106</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>112</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>103</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>45</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>109</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>109</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>110</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>106</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>112</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>103</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>45</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>109</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>109</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>110</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>106</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>97</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>Address.toUuidBytes</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>106</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>98</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>Address.toUuidBytes [114, 101, 106, 101, 99, 116, 101, 100, 58, 112, 97, 103, 101, 45, 99, 111, 109, 109, 97, 110, 100] == Address.toUuidBytes [114, 101, 106, 101, 99, 116, 101, 100, 58, 112, 97, 103, 101, 45, 99, 111, 109, 109, 97, 110, 100] &amp;&amp; Address.toUuidBytes [114, 101, 106, 101, 99, 116, 101, 100, 58, 97] != Address.toUuidBytes [114, 101, 106, 101, 99, 116, 101, 100, 58, 98]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([114,\,101,\,106,\,101,\,99,\,116,\,101,\,100,\,58,\,112,\,97,\,103,\,101,\,45,\,99,\,111,\,109,\,109,\,97,\,110,\,100]\right) = \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([114,\,101,\,106,\,101,\,99,\,116,\,101,\,100,\,58,\,112,\,97,\,103,\,101,\,45,\,99,\,111,\,109,\,109,\,97,\,110,\,100]\right) \land \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([114,\,101,\,106,\,101,\,99,\,116,\,101,\,100,\,58,\,97]\right) \neq \mathrm{Address.toUuidBytes}\mathopen{}\left([114,\,101,\,106,\,101,\,99,\,116,\,101,\,100,\,58,\,98]\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the rejected command gets a receipt: a refused command is content-addressed and documented, not silently dropp</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 44,100 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-mechanical-the_cardinality_claims_hold_of_any_four_symbol_alphabet">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 741</strong> (<code>the_cardinality_claims_hold_of_any_four_symbol_alphabet</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_mechanical_the_cardinality_claims_hold_of_any_four_symbol_alphabet">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><msup><mn>8</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>4 ^ 3 = 64 ∧ 2 ^ 6 = 64 ∧ 8 ^ 2 = 64 ∧ 4 ^ 3 = 2 ^ 6</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>4^{3} = 64 \land 2^{6} = 64 \land 8^{2} = 64 \land 4^{3} = 2^{6}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── THE BOLD CLAIMS OF THIS FILE, AND THE COMPUTATIONS THAT BREAK THEM ───────────────────────────────── Twenty-six theorems here carry names that CLAIM ABOUT THE WORLD — that DNA is the version itself, that the genetic code is the octave squared, that gravity holds prose and code and paths, that intentions are shown by receipts and not by role. They are stated boldly and they stay stated. What follows is the computation a critic runs against them, published here rather than left for someone to find. The claims fall into two classes and each class has one defeater, PROVED below rather than described. CLASS ONE — CARDINALITY. Sixteen decide arithmetic on counts: 4^3 = 64 beside DNA, 6 + 1 = 7 beside the creation week, 3 * 2 = 6 beside reading frames, 2/1 beside the octave. THE ARITHMETIC IS TRUE OF EVERY STRUCTURE WITH THOSE COUNTS. Four symbols in triples give sixty-four whether they are nucleotides, DNA bases, playing-card suits or nothing at all. The theorem decides the count; the NAME supplies the subject, and the subject is a choice a reader is free to reject. A critic substitutes any other four-symbol alphabet and the arithmetic does not move. CLASS TWO — REFLEXIVITY, and this defeater is the harder one. Ten compare an address with itself: `Address.toUuidBytes x == Address.toUuidBytes x`. THAT HOLDS FOR ANY FUNCTION WHATEVER, INCLUDING A CONSTANT ONE THAT THROWS ITS INPUT AWAY. It witnesses that addressing is deterministic on one input. It witnesses nothing about gravity, cells, sensors or intentions, and it would hold unchanged if the address function were replaced by `fun _ =&gt; []`. Both defeaters are decided here, so the limit is not a caveat in prose but a proposition the kernel checks.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

### Nim {#nim}

<p class="paper-src"><code>src/proof/nim.lean</code> · namespace <code>Nim</code> · 28 theorems</p>

Nim — Bouton's theorem and Sprague–Grundy, decided.


The ledger asserted these in TypeScript: that a Nim position is lost for the mover exactly when the XOR of
the heaps is zero, and that a single heap's Grundy value is its size. Both are real theorems with real
proofs; what is done here is to DECIDE them over a named finite board — every position with heaps up to a
bound — which is what `decide` can honestly deliver. It is not a proof for all heap sizes, and the range is
stated in each name rather than implied.

XOR is imported from Fnv rather than restated: it is the same fuel-bounded structural fold, built because
Nat's bitwise operations are well-founded and would drag `propext` into every theorem here. Its laws are
proved below for every a, b, c, on the standard axioms; the decided rows above stay as their instances.

<p class="paper-h">Definitions</p>

<pre class="thm-statement paper-defs"><code>N := 6</code></pre>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-bouton_two_heaps_lost_iff_xor_zero">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 763</strong> (<code>bouton_two_heaps_lost_iff_xor_zero</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_bouton_two_heaps_lost_iff_xor_zero">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>isLost</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>xorN</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range N).all (fun a =&gt; (List.range N).all (fun b =&gt; isLost a b == (xorN a b == 0)))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall a \in \{0,\dots,N-1\},\; \forall b \in \{0,\dots,N-1\},\; \mathrm{isLost}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b\right) = \mathrm{xorN}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b\right) = 0</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── BOUTON: a two-heap position is lost for the mover exactly when the heaps are equal — which is exactly when their XOR is zero. Decided over every position on the N×N board, N = 6. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-bouton_lost_iff_heaps_equal">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 764</strong> (<code>bouton_lost_iff_heaps_equal</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_bouton_lost_iff_heaps_equal">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>isLost</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range N).all (fun a =&gt; (List.range N).all (fun b =&gt; isLost a b == (a == b)))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall a \in \{0,\dots,N-1\},\; \forall b \in \{0,\dots,N-1\},\; \mathrm{isLost}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b\right) = a = b</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the same statement in its familiar form: lost exactly when the heaps are equal ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-lost_positions_are_exactly_the_diagonal">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 765</strong> (<code>lost_positions_are_exactly_the_diagonal</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_lost_positions_are_exactly_the_diagonal">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>⋃</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mi>isLost</mi><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(((List.range N).flatMap (fun a =&gt; (List.range N).map (fun b =&gt; (a, b)))).filter (fun p =&gt; isLost p.1 p.2)).length = N</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\{\, p \in \bigcup_{a \in \{0,\dots,N-1\}} \{\, \left(a,\,b\right) \mid b \in \{0,\dots,N-1\} \,\} \mid \mathrm{isLost}\mathopen{}\left(p_{1},\,p_{2}\right) \,\}\right| = N</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── NON-VACUITY: the losing positions are exactly the diagonal, so there are N of them among N² — neither everything nor nothing. (An earlier version fixed this count at 8 for an 8x8 board; when the board was reduced the kernel proved the statement FALSE rather than letting a stale constant pass. Tied to N now.) ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-grundy_of_a_single_heap_is_its_size">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 766</strong> (<code>grundy_of_a_single_heap_is_its_size</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_grundy_of_a_single_heap_is_its_size">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>grundy1</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range N).all (fun n =&gt; grundy1 (n + 1) n == n)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{0,\dots,N-1\},\; \mathrm{grundy1}\mathopen{}\left(n + 1,\,n\right) = n</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-grundy_of_two_heaps_is_the_xor">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 767</strong> (<code>grundy_of_two_heaps_is_the_xor</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_grundy_of_two_heaps_is_the_xor">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>xorN</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>grundy1</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>grundy1</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>xorN</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range N).all (fun a =&gt; (List.range N).all (fun b =&gt; (xorN (grundy1 (a + 1) a) (grundy1 (b + 1) b)) == xorN a b))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall a \in \{0,\dots,N-1\},\; \forall b \in \{0,\dots,N-1\},\; \mathrm{xorN}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{grundy1}\mathopen{}\left(a + 1,\,a\right),\,\mathrm{grundy1}\mathopen{}\left(b + 1,\,b\right)\right) = \mathrm{xorN}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── and the two-heap Grundy value is the XOR of the parts ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-xor_is_its_own_inverse">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 768</strong> (<code>xor_is_its_own_inverse</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_xor_is_its_own_inverse">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>xorN</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>xorN</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 16).all (fun a =&gt; (List.range 16).all (fun b =&gt; xorN (xorN a b) b == a))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall a \in \{0,\dots,15\},\; \forall b \in \{0,\dots,15\},\; \mathrm{xorN}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{xorN}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b\right),\,b\right) = a</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── XOR's algebra, which is why the theorem takes the form it does ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 256 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-xor_is_commutative">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 769</strong> (<code>xor_is_commutative</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_xor_is_commutative">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>xorN</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>xorN</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 16).all (fun a =&gt; (List.range 16).all (fun b =&gt; xorN a b == xorN b a))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall a \in \{0,\dots,15\},\; \forall b \in \{0,\dots,15\},\; \mathrm{xorN}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b\right) = \mathrm{xorN}\mathopen{}\left(b,\,a\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 256 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-xor_zero_is_identity">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 770</strong> (<code>xor_zero_is_identity</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_xor_zero_is_identity">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>31</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>xorN</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 32).all (fun a =&gt; xorN a 0 == a)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall a \in \{0,\dots,31\},\; \mathrm{xorN}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,0\right) = a</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 32 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-the_nim_sum_is_a_gf2_vector_addition">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 771</strong> (<code>the_nim_sum_is_a_gf2_vector_addition</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_the_nim_sum_is_a_gf2_vector_addition">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>xorN</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>xorN</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>xorN</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>xorN</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>xorN</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>xorN</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>xorN</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>xorN</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>xorN</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 16).all (fun a =&gt; (List.range 16).all (fun b =&gt; xorN a b == xorN b a)) ∧ (List.range 16).all (fun a =&gt; (List.range 16).all (fun b =&gt; (List.range 16).all (fun c =&gt; xorN (xorN a b) c == xorN a (xorN b c)))) ∧ (List.range 16).all (fun a =&gt; (List.range 16).all (fun b =&gt; xorN (xorN a b) b == a)) ∧ (List.range 16).all (fun a =&gt; xorN a 0 == a)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall a \in \{0,\dots,15\},\; \forall b \in \{0,\dots,15\},\; \mathrm{xorN}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b\right) = \mathrm{xorN}\mathopen{}\left(b,\,a\right) \land \forall a \in \{0,\dots,15\},\; \forall b \in \{0,\dots,15\},\; \forall c \in \{0,\dots,15\},\; \mathrm{xorN}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{xorN}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b\right),\,c\right) = \mathrm{xorN}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,\mathrm{xorN}\mathopen{}\left(b,\,c\right)\right) \land \forall a \in \{0,\dots,15\},\; \forall b \in \{0,\dots,15\},\; \mathrm{xorN}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{xorN}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b\right),\,b\right) = a \land \forall a \in \{0,\dots,15\},\; \mathrm{xorN}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,0\right) = a</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── THE NIM-SUM AS GF(2) VECTOR ADDITION, IN ONE PROPOSITION ───────────────────────────────────────────── `nim_sum_is_xor_gf2` claims the nim-sum IS GF(2) vector addition: commutative, associative and self-inverse. Associativity was the one property missing here — and the other three, though each decided above, are decided SEPARATELY. A claim is carried by a theorem that decides all of it or by none, and the ledger's supersededBy names exactly one key, so three quarters of a claim spread over three theorems carries nothing. The conjunction is the claim; the conjuncts standing alone are its parts, which is why both forms are here rather than one. Range 16 because the cube of it is walked.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 4,294,967,296 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-bouton_holds_at_every_heap_size_to_six">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 772</strong> (<code>bouton_holds_at_every_heap_size_to_six</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_bouton_holds_at_every_heap_size_to_six">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>isLost</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>xorN</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 7).all (fun a =&gt; (List.range 7).all (fun b =&gt; isLost a b == (xorN a b == 0)))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall a \in \{0,\dots,6\},\; \forall b \in \{0,\dots,6\},\; \mathrm{isLost}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b\right) = \mathrm{xorN}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b\right) = 0</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 49 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-the_xor_of_two_bits_is_their_sum_mod_two">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 773</strong> (<code>the_xor_of_two_bits_is_their_sum_mod_two</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_the_xor_of_two_bits_is_their_sum_mod_two">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ x y : Nat, (if x % 2 == y % 2 then 0 else 1) = (x + y) % 2</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── XOR's algebra for every a, b, c — no bound ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── xor_is_its_own_inverse and xor_is_commutative (a, b &lt; 16), xor_zero_is_identity (a &lt; 32) and the_nim_sum_is_a_gf2_vector_addition (a, b, c &lt; 16) were decided over a range; these prove them for every value. The fold's fuel is a + b + 1, which always suffices: once it exceeds either argument, more fuel changes nothing, so xorN reads the same at any sufficient fuel. Everything follows from one step — the low bit of a XOR is the sum of the low bits mod 2, and the rest is twice the XOR of the halves — by induction. Bouton's theorem itself is still decided over the N×N board above; a proof of it for every heap is a game-tree induction not done here.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-xor_commutes_at_every_fuel">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 774</strong> (<code>xor_commutes_at_every_fuel</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_xor_commutes_at_every_fuel">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ f a b : Nat, xorF f a b = xorF f b a</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-one_more_step_of_fuel_changes_nothing_once_it_exceeds_an_argument">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 775</strong> (<code>one_more_step_of_fuel_changes_nothing_once_it_exceeds_an_argument</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_one_more_step_of_fuel_changes_nothing_once_it_exceeds_an_argument">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ f a b : Nat, (a &lt; f ∨ b &lt; f) → xorF (f + 1) a b = xorF f a b</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-more_fuel_changes_nothing_once_it_exceeds_an_argument">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 776</strong> (<code>more_fuel_changes_nothing_once_it_exceeds_an_argument</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_more_fuel_changes_nothing_once_it_exceeds_an_argument">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ k f a b : Nat, (a &lt; f ∨ b &lt; f) → xorF (f + k) a b = xorF f a b</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-xor_reads_the_same_at_every_sufficient_fuel">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 777</strong> (<code>xor_reads_the_same_at_every_sufficient_fuel</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_xor_reads_the_same_at_every_sufficient_fuel">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ g a b : Nat, (a &lt; g ∨ b &lt; g) → xorN a b = xorF g a b</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-a_number_xored_with_itself_is_zero_at_every_fuel">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 778</strong> (<code>a_number_xored_with_itself_is_zero_at_every_fuel</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_a_number_xored_with_itself_is_zero_at_every_fuel">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ f b : Nat, xorF f b b = 0</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-xor_splits_off_its_lowest_bit">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 779</strong> (<code>xor_splits_off_its_lowest_bit</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_xor_splits_off_its_lowest_bit">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ g x c : Nat, 1 ≤ g → xorF (g + 1) x c = (x + c) % 2 + 2 * xorF g (x / 2) (c / 2)</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-xor_undoes_itself_when_the_fuel_suffices">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 780</strong> (<code>xor_undoes_itself_when_the_fuel_suffices</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_xor_undoes_itself_when_the_fuel_suffices">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ f a b g : Nat, (a &lt; f ∨ b &lt; f) → b &lt; g → xorF g (xorF f a b) b = a</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-xor_is_commutative_for_every_a_b">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 781</strong> (<code>xor_is_commutative_for_every_a_b</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_xor_is_commutative_for_every_a_b">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ a b : Nat, xorN a b = xorN b a</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-xor_zero_is_identity_for_every_a">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 782</strong> (<code>xor_zero_is_identity_for_every_a</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_xor_zero_is_identity_for_every_a">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ a : Nat, xorN a 0 = a</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-xor_is_its_own_inverse_for_every_a_b">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 783</strong> (<code>xor_is_its_own_inverse_for_every_a_b</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_xor_is_its_own_inverse_for_every_a_b">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ a b : Nat, xorN (xorN a b) b = a</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-xor_is_the_sum_of_the_bits_plus_twice_the_xor_of_the_halves">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 784</strong> (<code>xor_is_the_sum_of_the_bits_plus_twice_the_xor_of_the_halves</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_xor_is_the_sum_of_the_bits_plus_twice_the_xor_of_the_halves">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ a b : Nat, xorN a b = (a + b) % 2 + 2 * xorN (a / 2) (b / 2)</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-xor_is_associative_below_every_bound">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 785</strong> (<code>xor_is_associative_below_every_bound</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_xor_is_associative_below_every_bound">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ n a b c : Nat, a + b + c ≤ n → xorN (xorN a b) c = xorN a (xorN b c)</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-xor_is_associative_for_every_a_b_c">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 786</strong> (<code>xor_is_associative_for_every_a_b_c</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_xor_is_associative_for_every_a_b_c">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ a b c : Nat, xorN (xorN a b) c = xorN a (xorN b c)</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-the_nim_sum_is_a_gf2_vector_addition_for_every_a_b_c">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 787</strong> (<code>the_nim_sum_is_a_gf2_vector_addition_for_every_a_b_c</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_the_nim_sum_is_a_gf2_vector_addition_for_every_a_b_c">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ a b c : Nat, xorN a b = xorN b a ∧ xorN (xorN a b) c = xorN a (xorN b c) ∧ xorN (xorN a b) b = a ∧ xorN a 0 = a</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-a_number_xored_with_itself_is_zero_for_every_a">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 788</strong> (<code>a_number_xored_with_itself_is_zero_for_every_a</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_a_number_xored_with_itself_is_zero_for_every_a">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ a : Nat, xorN a a = 0</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── reflections, from the xor batch: each law beside its inverse (the 2×7 ↔ 1+6 wave) ── REFLECTIONS</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-xor_is_zero_only_on_equal_arguments_for_every_a_b">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 789</strong> (<code>xor_is_zero_only_on_equal_arguments_for_every_a_b</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_xor_is_zero_only_on_equal_arguments_for_every_a_b">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ a b : Nat, xorN a b = 0 ↔ a = b</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-nim-the_halves_and_the_low_bit_read_back_from_the_xor_for_every_a_b">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 790</strong> (<code>the_halves_and_the_low_bit_read_back_from_the_xor_for_every_a_b</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_nim_the_halves_and_the_low_bit_read_back_from_the_xor_for_every_a_b">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ a b : Nat, xorN a b / 2 = xorN (a / 2) (b / 2) ∧ xorN a b % 2 = (a + b) % 2</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>


### Digit reversal {#reversal}

<p class="paper-src"><code>src/proof/reversal.lean</code> · namespace <code>Reversal</code> · 30 theorems</p>

Digit reversal — arithmetic, not string handling.


An earlier pass called this family "not generatable: needs string manipulation, no small decidable form".
That was wrong. A digit is arithmetic — n % 10 and n / 10 — so reversal is a structural fold with no strings
anywhere. The mathematics is real too: the digital root is a function of the digit SUM, and reversal is a
permutation of the digits, so invariance under reversal is a THEOREM rather than a coincidence. That is
exactly what makes emirps — primes whose reversal is also prime — a meaningful class rather than a curio.
No axioms, no Mathlib, no sorry.

<p class="paper-h">Definitions</p>

<pre class="thm-statement paper-defs"><code>settledHere := 8</code></pre>

<div class="thm" id="thm-reversal-reversal_preserves_digit_sum">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 791</strong> (<code>reversal_preserves_digit_sum</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_reversal_reversal_preserves_digit_sum">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>300</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>digitSum</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>reverseNum</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>digitSum</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 300).all (fun n =&gt; digitSum (reverseNum n) == digitSum n)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{1,\dots,300\},\; \mathrm{digitSum}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{reverseNum}\mathopen{}\left(n\right)\right) = \mathrm{digitSum}\mathopen{}\left(n\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── reversal is a permutation of the digits, so it preserves their sum ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 300 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-reversal-digital_root_is_invariant_under_reversal">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 792</strong> (<code>digital_root_is_invariant_under_reversal</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_reversal_digital_root_is_invariant_under_reversal">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>300</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>reverseNum</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 300).all (fun n =&gt; (reverseNum n) % 9 == n % 9)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{1,\dots,300\},\; \mathrm{reverseNum}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) \bmod 9 = n \bmod 9</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── and therefore preserves the residue mod 9 — the digital root is invariant under reversal ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 300 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-reversal-the_ledger_reversal_cases">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 793</strong> (<code>the_ledger_reversal_cases</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_reversal_the_ledger_reversal_cases">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>reverseNum</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>reverseNum</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>45</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>45</mn><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>reverseNum</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>123</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>123</mn><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>reverseNum</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1234</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1234</mn><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>reverseNum</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4321</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>4321</mn><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>reverseNum</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9080</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>9080</mn><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(reverseNum 12) % 9 == 12 % 9 ∧ (reverseNum 45) % 9 == 45 % 9 ∧ (reverseNum 123) % 9 == 123 % 9 ∧ (reverseNum 1234) % 9 == 1234 % 9 ∧ (reverseNum 4321) % 9 == 4321 % 9 ∧ (reverseNum 9080) % 9 == 9080 % 9</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{reverseNum}\mathopen{}\left(12\right) \bmod 9 = 12 \bmod 9 \land \mathrm{reverseNum}\mathopen{}\left(45\right) \bmod 9 = 45 \bmod 9 \land \mathrm{reverseNum}\mathopen{}\left(123\right) \bmod 9 = 123 \bmod 9 \land \mathrm{reverseNum}\mathopen{}\left(1234\right) \bmod 9 = 1234 \bmod 9 \land \mathrm{reverseNum}\mathopen{}\left(4321\right) \bmod 9 = 4321 \bmod 9 \land \mathrm{reverseNum}\mathopen{}\left(9080\right) \bmod 9 = 9080 \bmod 9</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the ledger's own cases, now stated rather than asserted ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-reversal-reversal_is_not_the_identity">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 794</strong> (<code>reversal_is_not_the_identity</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_reversal_reversal_is_not_the_identity">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>reverseNum</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>¬ ((List.range' 10 90).all (fun n =&gt; reverseNum n == n))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\lnot \forall n \in \{10,\dots,99\},\; \mathrm{reverseNum}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) = n</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── NON-VACUITY: reversal genuinely moves the number, so the invariance is not about a fixed point ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 90 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-reversal-palindromes_are_the_fixed_points">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 795</strong> (<code>palindromes_are_the_fixed_points</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_reversal_palindromes_are_the_fixed_points">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>reverseNum</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>((List.range' 10 90).filter (fun n =&gt; reverseNum n == n)).length = 9</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\{\, n \in \{10,\dots,99\} \mid \mathrm{reverseNum}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) = n \,\}\right| = 9</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── palindromes are exactly the fixed points, and there are nine of them below 100 ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 90 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-reversal-emirps_exist_below_one_hundred">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 796</strong> (<code>emirps_exist_below_one_hundred</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_reversal_emirps_exist_below_one_hundred">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>isPrime</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mi>isPrime</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>reverseNum</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>reverseNum</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>((List.range' 10 90).filter (fun n =&gt; isPrime n &amp;&amp; isPrime (reverseNum n) &amp;&amp; reverseNum n != n)).length &gt; 0</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\{\, n \in \{10,\dots,99\} \mid \mathrm{isPrime}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) \land \mathrm{isPrime}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{reverseNum}\mathopen{}\left(n\right)\right) \land \mathrm{reverseNum}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) \neq n \,\}\right| &gt; 0</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 90 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-reversal-reversal_does_not_preserve_primality">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 797</strong> (<code>reversal_does_not_preserve_primality</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_reversal_reversal_does_not_preserve_primality">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>isPrime</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>isPrime</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>reverseNum</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>¬ ((List.range' 10 90).all (fun n =&gt; isPrime n == isPrime (reverseNum n)))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\lnot \forall n \in \{10,\dots,99\},\; \mathrm{isPrime}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) = \mathrm{isPrime}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{reverseNum}\mathopen{}\left(n\right)\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── and reversal does NOT preserve primality in general: the boundary that makes emirps a real class ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 90 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-reversal-reversal_is_involutive_exactly_off_the_trailing_zeros">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 798</strong> (<code>reversal_is_involutive_exactly_off_the_trailing_zeros</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_reversal_reversal_is_involutive_exactly_off_the_trailing_zeros">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>300</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>reverseNum</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>reverseNum</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 300).all (fun n =&gt; (reverseNum (reverseNum n) == n) == (n % 10 != 0))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{1,\dots,300\},\; \mathrm{reverseNum}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{reverseNum}\mathopen{}\left(n\right)\right) = n = n \bmod 10 \neq 0</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── WHERE REVERSAL STOPS BEING AN INVOLUTION. Reversing twice usually returns the number — but not always: a trailing zero is destroyed by the first reversal and cannot be restored by the second (120 → 021 = 21 → 12). So reversal is self-inverse EXACTLY on the numbers with no trailing zero, and the iff is decided in both directions across the range, not asserted for the convenient half. The exception is the whole content of the theorem: an involution that quietly fails on a tenth of its domain is not an involution.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 300 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-reversal-reversal_settles_its_range">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 799</strong> (<code>reversal_settles_its_range</code>)<span class="thm-uncited">not sealed — settled by <code>rfl</code>, not exhausted</span>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>settledHere</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>settledHere = 8</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{settledHere} = 8</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>rfl</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-reversal-foldl_add_start">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 800</strong> (<code>foldl_add_start</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_reversal_foldl_add_start">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ (l : List Nat) (a : Nat), l.foldl (· + ·) a = a + l.foldl (· + ·) 0</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the capped rows above, proved for every value by induction — no bound ──────────────────────────────────── casting out nines, in general: a number, its digit sum and its reversal share their residue mod 9.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-reversal-the_digits_sum_to_the_number_mod_nine_when_the_fuel_covers_them">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 801</strong> (<code>the_digits_sum_to_the_number_mod_nine_when_the_fuel_covers_them</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_reversal_the_digits_sum_to_the_number_mod_nine_when_the_fuel_covers_them">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ f n : Nat, n &lt; 10 ^ f → (digitsF f n).foldl (· + ·) 0 % 9 = n % 9</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-reversal-a_number_is_below_ten_to_its_own_successor">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 802</strong> (<code>a_number_is_below_ten_to_its_own_successor</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_reversal_a_number_is_below_ten_to_its_own_successor">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ n : Nat, n &lt; 10 ^ (n + 1)</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-reversal-the_digit_sum_has_the_residue_of_the_number_mod_nine_for_every_n">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 803</strong> (<code>the_digit_sum_has_the_residue_of_the_number_mod_nine_for_every_n</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_reversal_the_digit_sum_has_the_residue_of_the_number_mod_nine_for_every_n">sealed</a>.</p>

</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-reversal-folding_by_ten_keeps_the_residue_of_the_digit_sum">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 804</strong> (<code>folding_by_ten_keeps_the_residue_of_the_digit_sum</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_reversal_folding_by_ten_keeps_the_residue_of_the_digit_sum">sealed</a>.</p>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>∀ (l : List Nat) (a : Nat), (l.foldl (fun a d =&gt; a * 10 + d) a) % 9 = (a + l.foldl (· + ·) 0) % 9</code></pre>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by
  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-reversal-reversal_keeps_the_residue_mod_nine_for_every_n">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 805</strong> (<code>reversal_keeps_the_residue_mod_nine_for_every_n</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_reversal_reversal_keeps_the_residue_mod_nine_for_every_n">sealed</a>.</p>

  intro</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-reversal-the_digits_of_the_reversal_are_the_reversed_digits">
